/nl/course/2026/LBVP26IBP1C.content:
This 10 EC group-based module enables students to transform an innovative international business idea into a viable business plan based on sound primary and secondary research.
Students integrate marketing, financial, managerial, legal, and sustainability considerations to evaluate feasibility and responsible value creation. The course contributes to IBS’s strategic focus areas by fostering a global mindset through international opportunity evaluation, strengthening entrepreneurial competences, and embedding sustainability aligned with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).
The module concludes with a professional individual defence.
And as an extra: some selected teams present their business concepts to external stakeholders in a “Dragon’s Den” simulation to reflect real-world entrepreneurial conditions.

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26IBC1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, students develop professional communication skills by creating and sharing business-related outputs within international business contexts.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can communicate in a clear, well-structured, and professional manner to identify international business opportunities and propose strategies that create sustainable, multi-sided value for stakeholders.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, students engage in planning, reflection, and peer-feedback activities related to professional communication in a business context.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can plan, communicate, and reflect on professional business contributions that support sustainable international business practices and organisational transformation.
PLO3: Relationship Management
In this course, students practise structured and appropriate use of English for professional communication in an international business context.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can apply structured and formal business English to communicate responsibly and effectively with diverse stakeholders, using clear organisation, accurate language, an appropriate professional tone, and cultural sensitivity.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26IBC1C.content:
Business Report writing:
Students will know how to organise sources, using APA, and how to integrate these in business reports. In addition, students will learn how business reports are built up and structured and written, using formal business English. Report writing can contribute to strategic themes of sustainability, global mindset, and entrepreneurship. Integrating with the business consulting project, students research and describe innovative solutions to sustainability challenges (SDG7). Overall, this can promote critical thinking, effective communication, collaboration, and creativity, and allow students to apply these skills to real-world challenges.
Presenting:
Students present, as an independent entrepreneur, (a niche) product and its expected sales projection and can present this professionally to potential investors. Students use professional business English and apply the presentation style and structure addressed, while using appropriate (audio) visual material. Students who learn to present their ideas in a clear and concise manner can effectively communicate with diverse audiences and work collaboratively with people from different backgrounds and cultures. This can enhance their global mindset and facilitate their ability to work in international contexts.

metadata.Naam: Intercultural and Professional Skills in International Business 1

/nl/course/2026/LBVP26IPS1C.outcomes:
PLO3:
Relationship Management
In this course, students engage in interactive and reflective learning activities to analyze intercultural business situations and formulate appropriate responses.
Learning Line:
Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can mitigate the pitfalls of cultural differences in business and social contexts by displaying willingness to work with people from diverse cultural backgrounds and in different countries in order to cultivate and manage relationships responsibly with culturally diverse stakeholders and achieve mutual business goals.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, students complete reflective exercises and activities to enhance their self-management and professionalism.
Learning Line:
Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can reflect on their personal development to enhance self-management and professionalism for the benefit of themselves, the organisation, and the field of international business.
/nl/course/2026/LBVP26IPS1C.content: This course prepares students to add value to international business and society by developing essential life and career skills, commonly referred to as 21st-century skills, through interactive workshops. The seminars aim to cultivate business professionals with a global mindset by guiding students through several key steps. First, students enhance their awareness of their own cultural assumptions and begin to recognize differences in others’ perspectives. They are encouraged to interpret the experiences and behaviours of others through their own cultural lens and respond appropriately. The course also emphasizes the importance of leveraging cultural differences in verbal and non-verbal communication to foster shared understanding. SDG 10.

metadata.Naam: Financial Statement Analysis of a Multinational Enterprise

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSA1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student learns to apply an intermediate understanding of finance, accounting, and supply chain management to analyse how firms create value through financial performance, capital structure, and operational efficiency.
Learning Line: Economics, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can interpret financial statements and ratio analyses to assess a company’s financial health, capital structure, and potential for long-term value creation.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can evaluate how inbound logistics influence performance and propose straightforward improvements to enhance value creation.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, the student learns to apply intermediate financial, operational, and sustainability insights to identify improvement opportunities and provide responsible, evidence-based recommendations for business transformation.
Learning Line: Economic, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can analyse financial data and external business information to draw conclusions about a company’s future financial performance and formulate realistic, data-driven recommendations for improvement.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can use financial and operational information to propose actions that optimise the cash conversion cycle and strengthen sustainable supply chain performance.
Learning Line: Sustainability and Societal Impact:
CLO3: The student can evaluate a company’s sustainability developments and apply the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework to formulate value-adding recommendations for responsible business transformation.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSA1C.content: This course focuses on the financial and operational analysis of a multinational enterprise. Working in teams, students assess financial performance, capital structure, and the cash conversion cycle, and develop improvement proposals that integrate inbound logistics. The international company context supports a global mindset by strengthening analytical skills in cross-border business environments. The course connects to sustainability and social impact through the evaluation of corporate sustainability strategies and their financial implications, with strongest alignment to SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSM1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student develops an intermediate understanding of financial and supply chain concepts to evaluate how firms create and sustain value through financial decisions and inbound logistics management.
Learning Line: Economics, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can analyse financial statements and key performance indicators, including ratio and working capital analysis, to assess a company’s financial position and value creation potential.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can explain and evaluate how inbound logistics and procurement decisions affect the efficiency, responsiveness, and financial health of an organisation.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, the student learns to apply intermediate financial and operational insights to improve processes and contribute to responsible, data-informed business transformation.
Learning Line: Economics, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can apply financial analysis and working capital management techniques to identify opportunities for improving liquidity, leverage, and sustainable business performance.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can analyse and recommend improvements to inbound logistics and inventory processes to enhance operational effectiveness and support sustainable supply chain transformation.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSM1A.content: This course integrates managerial finance, financial accounting, and inbound logistics to analyse how financial and supply chain decisions jointly influence organisational performance. Students develop skills in ratio analysis, working capital management, and inventory decision-making to evaluate liquidity, efficiency, and value creation. The course supports entrepreneurship by strengthening data-informed financial and operational decision-making. It connects to sustainability and social impact through responsible resource use and sustainable supply chain practices, aligning most strongly with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26ISC1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student develops an intermediate understanding of supply chain and related business functions to make informed, data-driven decisions in a complex international business environment.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO1: The student can analyse dynamic international supply chain environments and apply supply chain and logistics principles to make well-justified operational and strategic decisions in line with organisational goals.
Learning Line: Management:
CLO2: The student can interpret and apply financial, marketing, and human resource information to support balanced, cross-functional decisions that align with the company’s overall strategy.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, the student learns to integrate financial, operational, and human perspectives to improve organisational performance and work effectively in diverse, team-based business settings.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO1: The student can monitor and evaluate supply chain and financial performance indicators to identify improvement opportunities and propose actions that strengthen operational efficiency and responsiveness.
Learning Line: Management:
CLO2: The student can synthesise insights from finance, marketing, and HRM to contribute to strategic alignment and responsible business transformation in an international context.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26ISC1C.content: This course uses a competitive simulation game to immerse students in managing supply chains across domestic and international markets. Teams make integrated decisions in supply chain management, finance, marketing, and HRM within a dynamic and uncertain environment. The international scope of the simulation strengthens a global mindset by developing intercultural awareness, collaboration, and communication in diverse teams. The course supports entrepreneurship by fostering strategic thinking and coordinated decision-making across business functions. Sustainability and social impact are addressed indirectly through responsible performance management in complex, resource-constrained business settings, with strongest relevance to SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

metadata.Naam: Financial and Supply Chain Decision Mak

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSD1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student further develops an intermediate understanding of finance, accounting, and supply chain management to evaluate how organisations create and sustain value through investment, operational, and logistical decisions.
Learning Line: Economics, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can apply capital budgeting and cost accounting techniques to evaluate the financial feasibility and value creation potential of business activities.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can analyse outbound logistics and demand forecasting data to design efficient and customer-oriented supply chain processes that support organisational goals.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, the student learns to apply intermediate financial, operational, and sustainability insights to improve business processes and promote responsible transformation.
Learning Line: Economics, Finance & Accounting:
CLO1: The student can analyse financial information to identify and explain performance gaps and propose actions that improve operational and financial efficiency.
Learning Line: Operations and Supply Chain:
CLO2: The student can evaluate supply chain performance and propose actions to enhance efficiency, resilience, and responsiveness under conditions of uncertainty.
Learning Line: Sustainability and Societal Impact:
CLO3: The student can explain and apply corporate responsibility and sustainability frameworks to align financial and supply chain decisions with ethical, social, and environmental objectives.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FSD1A.content: This course integrates financial & managerial accounting, supply chain management and corporate social responsibility to examine how investment, production, and logistics decisions affect sustainable organisational performance and customer service. Students develop skills in capital budgeting, cost and variance analysis, demand forecasting, and supply chain performance management under uncertainty. The course connects to entrepreneurship by supporting informed operational and investment decisions. It has a strong link to sustainability and social impact through corporate responsibility in supply chain planning and control, aligning most strongly with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure).

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FRP1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, the student develops an intermediate understanding of research and communication to investigate real-world international business challenges and communicate insights effectively to professional audiences.
Learning line: Research & Data Analytics:
• CLO1: The student can design and conduct applied research using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods to analyse complex international business problems.
Learning line: Global Mindset and Professional Development:
• CLO2: The student can communicate complex information clearly, coherently, and professionally, demonstrating critical and analytical use of language in an international business context.
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, the student learns to apply evidence-based insights to recommend feasible and responsible solutions for organisational improvement and sustainable value creation.
Learning line: Research & Data Analytics:
• CLO1: The student can apply analytical and interpretive skills to generate valid conclusions from business data and propose data-driven recommendations for improvement.
Learning line: Global Mindset and Professional Development:
• CLO2: The student can convey research-based insights and recommendations in a clear, structured, and professional manner to support responsible organizational decision-making.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26FRP1C.content: This course develops students’ ability to investigate and communicate solutions to real-world international business challenges. Students design and conduct applied research using qualitative and quantitative methods, and critically analyze current business issues related to law, economics, ethics, sustainability, and innovation. A strong global mindset is fostered through professional communication tailored to international audiences. The course connects to sustainability and social impact by emphasizing responsible, evidence-based decision-making and sustainable value creation, aligning most strongly with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

They can express opinions, describe experiences, and handle most situations that may arise while traveling. They begin to produce more connected speech and write short texts with some detail and coherence.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, students develop intermediate proficiency in the foreign language and continuously deepen their understanding of the foreign culture to navigate complex international contexts and enhance their professional self-management.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students critically reflect on how language and cultural skills support their self-management and professional growth.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26SPA3C.content: Learning a foreign language helps students become business professionals with a global mindset, as it will allow them to connect with people from another culture. By speaking another language and understanding another culture, they can break down the barriers of communication, putting themselves at a huge advantage as a business professional, next to experiencing a new world view and discovering new concepts.

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26MES1C.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
The IB professional defines international business opportunities and recommends possible strategies for the organisation to create sustainable value for stakeholders.
To identify and capture international marketing opportunities (PLO1), students focus on the practical application of market intelligence and strategic planning for a real-world organization. This course bridges the gap between theoretical analysis and actionable growth strategies, teaching students how to evaluate a company's readiness for global expansion and formulate a data-driven path for foreign market entry.
Learning Line: Marketing
CLO 1: Apply marketing theories to evaluate business opportunities, analysing market fit, entry modes, and segmentation–targeting decisions.
Learning line: Research & Data Analytics
CLO 2: Develop and justify a data-informed market entry plan that aligns company capabilities with target market dynamics and customer needs.
Learning Line: Entrepreneurship
CLO 3: Demonstrate an entrepreneurial mindset by generating innovative, feasible, and value-creating recommendations for international expansion.
PLO2: Business Transformation
Learning line: Research & Data Analytics
CLO 1: Demonstrate professional consulting competencies through stakeholder collaboration and data-driven decision-making.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, students analyse the legal context of an international market entry strategy for a real company, identifying potential risks and obligations, and develop a reasoned approach.
Learning line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can apply international legal knowledge to address the legal risks and obligations involved in a real-world market entry scenario, demonstrating professional judgement and decision-making in complex business environments.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26MES1C.content:
This course teaches students how to conduct international market research for a real-world organization. Effective collaboration and communication between students and organizations is expected.
Students analyse the strategic fit between an organization’s products and the international environment to justify their choice of market entry mode, positioning, and marketing mix. This planning process incorporates a deep understanding of underlying political and legal factors, specific regulatory requirements, and the management of legal liability.
Students consider the sustainable and ethical considerations of international expansion, which is linked to SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production.

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IMM1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
Learning Line: Marketing
To identify and capture international marketing opportunities (PLO1), students develop advanced knowledge of international marketing strategy and global market dynamics. The course deepens students’ understanding of how macro-economic developments, international trade structures, and digital trends shape strategic marketing decisions.
CLO1: Students understand the theoretical foundations of international marketing in foreign market development.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, students critically analyze international legal frameworks and the rules-based world order, exploring the political and legal complexities of cross-border business, and engage in structured debate and discussion to develop professional judgement, reasoning skills, and a nuanced understanding of international business law.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students understand relevant legal and regulatory frameworks and demonstrate awareness of compliance requirements and institutional constraints affecting business decisions.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IMM1A.content: This course examines international marketing strategy and international law within the context of global business. Students analyze international market segmentation, targeting and positioning, market entry strategies, and marketing mix decisions, alongside the legal frameworks governing cross-border trade, including private international law and the rules-based international order. The course strengthens a global mindset by exploring how strategic marketing decisions operate within diverse legal and political contexts. Sustainability is addressed through critical evaluation of responsible market participation and legal governance, aligning particularly with SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions).

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26ITM1C.outcomes:
PLO2: Business Transformation
In this course, students learn to design and develop a coherent international talent management plan that supports organizational objectives and contributes to organizational development.
Learning line: Management
CLO1
: Students can design an integrated talent management framework that aligns workforce planning, recruitment and selection, development, and performance management with organizational objectives.
CLO2
: Students can justify proposed talent management interventions based on organizational analysis and identified development needs.
PLO 3: Relationship Management
In this course, students learn to structure talent management systems that regulate and support emPLOyment relationships within international organizations.
Learning line: Management
CLO1
: Students can analyze how talent management policies influence emPLOyment relationships and organizational processes.
CLO2
: Students can integrate human resource and intercultural considerations into a coherent and internally consistent talent management proposal.
PLO 4: Self-Management
In this course, students develop professional collaboration and project execution skills in a team-based setting.
Learning line: Global Mindset and Professional Development
CLO1
: Students can contribute effectively to a team-based project by fulfilling assigned roles and responsibilities in the development of a talent management plan.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26ITM1C.content:
This course focuses on developing an international talent management plan within a project-based learning environment. Working in teams, students design a coherent framework integrating workforce planning, recruitment and selection, development, and performance management. They translate HRM theory into structured and feasible talent management solutions, with emphasis on system coherence, organizational alignment, and practical implementation.
This course supports the SDG8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) by promoting strategic talent development, productive employment practices, and sustainable organizational performance in international contexts.

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IPM1A.outcomes:
PLO1: International Business Opportunities
In this course, students learn to understand how human resource management systems contribute to organizational performance and strategic alignment in international contexts.
Learning line: Management
CLO1
: Students can explain how strategic human resource management supports organizational goals and performance.
CLO2
: Students can analyze how workforce planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, and performance management operate within diverse organizational environments.
PLO 3: Relationship Management
In this course, students learn to apply intercultural and human resource management theories to analyze managerial and organizational processes in culturally diverse settings.
Learning line: Management
CLO1
: Students can apply cultural frameworks (e.g., national culture dimensions and intercultural communication models) to analyze differences in managerial practices.
CLO2
: Students can explain how cultural values influence leadership, communication, HR policies, and organizational behavior in international organizations.
PLO 4: Self-Management
In this course, students develop awareness of cultural assumptions and their implications for managerial practice.
Learning line: Global Mindset and Professional Development
CLO1
: Students can critically reflect on cultural assumptions and their influence on managerial perception and decision-making.
CLO2
: Students can demonstrate awareness of intercultural challenges in professional contexts and explain strategies for effective cross-cultural interaction.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IPM1A.content:
This course examines people management in culturally diverse organizational contexts by integrating human resource management and intercultural management theory. Students explore how organizations design core HR processes and how cultural differences shape leadership, communication, and organizational behavior. Through lectures and seminars, they apply theoretical frameworks to contemporary international business situations.
This course supports the SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) by promoting inclusive HR practices, culturally responsive leadership, and responsible people management that enhance productive employment and sustainable organizational performance.

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26CDC1C.outcomes:
PLO3: Relationship Management
In this course, students deliver a service for the community. Students will apply knowledge of business etiquette and interpersonal skills to secure a community service role and complete the service while collaborating effectively with individuals from diverse roles, disciplines, and cultures.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can reflect on their collaboration with people from different backgrounds and reflect on their personal growth.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, while completing the community service role, students apply their planning and organization skills, and self-motivation skills, to go through the process of job solicitation, task execution and acquisition of feedback in a protected environment with a reflection moment at the end of the service. Students will also work on their personal branding by creating products for personal presentation in the job market.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can create professional products for personal presentations in the job market.
CLO2: Students can communicate professionally, digitally and live, verbal and non-verbal and reflect on their professional development.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26CDC1C.content: This course allows students to continue working on their professional skills development. The students engage in community service and build a professional presence in a global business environment with the aim of securing a suitable internship. The course aligns with SDG4 (Quality Education) by facilitating skills for personal growth and employability.

metadata.Naam: Intercultural and Professional Skills in Business 2

/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IPS2C.outcomes:
PLO3: Relationship Management
In this course, students critically analyse intercultural business situations and apply their learning by designing and facilitating interactive workshops, focusing on mitigating cultural misunderstandings and managing professional relationships responsibly.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can analyze and mitigate the pitfalls of cultural differences in business and social contexts to cultivate and manage relationships responsibly with culturally diverse stakeholders.
PLO4: Self-Management
In this course, students critically reflect on their personal development and apply intercultural insights through interactive and reflective activities, developing a structured personal learning plan to enhance self-management and professionalism.
Learning Line: Global mindset and professional development
CLO1: Students can critically reflect on their personal development and apply intercultural insights to a personal learning plan, enhancing self-management and professionalism.
/nl/course/2026/LBVB26IPS2C.content:
Intercultural and Professional Skills in Business (IPS2) aims to develop students’ competencies of relationship management and self-management through two paths of the learning journey.
During the first path of the IPS2 learning journey, students work in teams to develop and deliver a professional workshop to train peers. The workshop is planned and organized based on students’ different training needs related to intercultural competence. During the second path of the IPS2 learning journey, students work individually to develop a personal intercultural learning plan for either their year-abroad or exchange to IBS.
IPS2 is related to SDG 4 (Quality education) and Global Mindset. During this module, students embrace SDG target 4.5 (Eliminate all discrimination in education) and develop a global mindset by enhancing intercultural competence and sensitivity, facilitating diversity and inclusion, addressing discrimination and stereotypes, and providing intercultural competence training to peers.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25SCM1C.outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to :
CLO1: Critically analyse current supply chain challenges, such as delays in invoice processing, long cash-to-cash cycles, and inefficient inventory management, demonstrating an enhanced awareness and understanding of these issues. (PLO1)
CLO2: Systematically and creatively apply relevant supply chain theories and techniques learned from course literature, including textbooks, scientific articles, and company reports, in both individual and collaborative assignments to generate and interpret new knowledge within the field. (PLO2)
CLO3: Analyse complex supply chain problems under conditions of uncertainty and with limited or potentially biased industry and company-specific data, enabling informed decision-making. (PLO3).
CLO4: Evaluate supply chain problems at strategic, tactical, and operational levels and develop appropriate solutions to effectively address these issues. (PLO4, PLO5).
CLO5: Proactively identify existing and potential problems within supply chains and critically evaluate effective methodologies for their resolution. (PLO5)

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25HRM1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Global Mindset and Sustainability
This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the policies, practices, and challenges involved in managing human resources in multinational enterprises (MNEs) operating in a globalized environment.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25FMA1C.outcomes:
After completing the course the students:
•            FMA1 have gained an overview of and insight into the various theories in the fields of International Financial Management & Accounting, at a level which allows them to reflect critically on the literature dealing with counselling in those fields PLO1
•            FMA2 have gained insight into the several tools and strategies relating to the diagnosis and analysis of various types of complex management questions at a level which allows them employment in finance- related, knowledge-intensive departments, effectively applying theoretical concepts PLO2
•            FMA3 be able to use these tools and strategies in practice and to report on them orally and in writing PLO3
•            FMA4 be able to demonstrate the ability to recognize and address changes of strategic importance for the organization due to new economic realities and demonstrate the ability to use financial accounting and financial management tools to transform business processes PLO4
•            FMA5 have gained the knowledge to critically evaluate the validity and relevance of new theories and practices in the field of financial accounting and financial management and explore the possibly to extrapolate these into new approaches to management practice PLO
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25FMA1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas:
Entrepreneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
The course provides students at graduate levels with knowledge, skills and insights in contemporary topics and issues regarding corporate finance, financial controlling systems, ethical accounting and finance and financial management. Not only principles and theories are the studying issues, but integration of these issues is offered with vocational business disciplines in a global setting.
Following items are of particular interest:
Responsibility Centers: revenue and expense centers
Profit Centers, Conditions for Delegating Proﬁt Responsibility, Business Units as Proﬁt Centers
Transfer Pricing, Constraints on Sourcing, Upstream Fixed Costs and Proﬁts
Measuring and Controlling Assets Employed, Structure of the Analysis, EVA vs. ROI, Additional Considerations in Evaluating Managers, Managing risks
Evaluating the Economic Performance of the Entity
New economic realities and emerging trends in the financial sector
Decentralization and outsourcing, profitability vs. corporate social responsibility
The course focus on the role of the manager:
to assess and monitor the (global) organization
act as a successful financial consultant
link cultural differences with strategic decisions
promote a holistic vision that aside profitability considerers environmental and social impact of an organization
SDG’s covered: 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25IMA1C.outcomes:
The course learning outcomes are:
IMA1: Analyze and apply advanced knowledge of marketing-related problems and critically evaluate current challenges, trends and new insights which are at the forefront of international business and management research and practice.
[Refers to PLO1]
IMA2: Apply knowledge and skills related to marketing environment, and its core aspects linked to product, price, place and promotion decisions (accordingly, linked to the value creation, vale capture, value delivery and value communication), together with a practical understanding of how established techniques of market research are used to gather and interpret data about international business and management.
[Refers to PLO2]
IMA3: Select and critically evaluate international business-related research publications of relevance to international marketing within internationally operating business and on the basis of historical and cultural insights.
[Refers to PLO3]
IMA4: Reflects on social and ethical responsibilities within operating in multidisciplinary and multicultural business and operates effectively, professionally and ethically in these organisations.
[Refers to PLO6]
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25IMA1C.content:
Strategic Focus Area:
Entrepreneurship
This course provides an advanced approach to the fundamentals of International Marketing Management and is based on a combination of lectures and discussions, business cases, videos, outside speakers, and country snapshots. Students will learn the scope and challenge of international marketing; the dynamic environment of international trade; the influence of the culture once doing business at the international level; political, legal, and business systems of international markets; the global market opportunities; and the ways to develop international marketing strategies.
The course covers the following topics:
Introduction to innovative marketing in modern organisations.
Marketing environment and market analysis.
Market Research.
Buyer Behaviour (both on a consumer and organisational level).
Segmentation, Targeting and Positioning.
Product (value creation).
Price (value capture).
Place (value delivery).
Promotion (value communication).
Final Project Review Session.
The module contributes to the Sustainable Development Goals as set by the UN, and in particular to the SDG12 (Responsible Production and Consumption) and engages the participants to get involved in Hanze activities on SDG’s.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25SDB1C.outcomes:
After completing the course, the student is able to:
assess the theoretical importance and practical applicability of major theories of decision-making and their application in complex and uncertain international politico-economic environments (Contributes to PLOs 1,3)
evaluate the emotional, moral and cognitive dimensions of the executive exercise of governance  (Contributes to PLOs 3,4)
analyse and appraise the institutional environment and the incentives of decision-making in a large multi-national corporation against the backdrop of Sustainability and Circular Economy norms and values (Contributes to PLOs 6, 7, 8)
create appropriate approaches to address stakeholder problems and exercise ethical judgment (Contributes to PLOs 5, 7, 8)
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25SDB1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Global Mindset, Sustainability
This module consists of a series of lectures/seminars, in which advanced theoretical knowledge will be provided about decision-making in complex and uncertain environments in international business. Next to that, the institutional environment, geopolitics and geo-economics, and incentives determining decision-making in a large corporation as well as normative paradigms like Sustainability and the Circular Economy are analyzed.

metadata.Toetsen: Inter. Strategic Management - Computer, organisatie ToetsCentrum

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25STM1.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Global Mindset & Sustainability
The course International Strategic Management covers all three dimensions of strategic management (process, content and context) and deals with a wide range of issues on each dimension.
As the course aims to go beyond understanding and applying basic tools and concepts, students are challenged to understand more complex phenomena and to critically reflect upon them. This is reinforced by not shielding students from the uncertainties, inconsistencies and disputes within the field of strategic management.
This course contributes to the following SDG’s: 1, 8, 9 & 12.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25ISB1C.outcomes:
Upon a successful completion of the course ISB, participants will be able to:
• ISB1: Learn on working in an international team of upcoming professionals from multiple universities in both on- and off-line setting (contributes to PLO 7 & 8)
• ISB2: To analyze and apply on the impact on the latest insights on sustainability e.g. circular economy, sufficiency and de-growth theories, models and concepts on contemporary business practices (contributes to PLO 1, 2, 3, 4 & 6)
• ISB3: To identify sustainable and actionable strategies for businesses to enhance their sustainable and competitive advantage (contributes to PLO 1, 3 & 6)
• ISN4: To evaluate and decide on strategies on solving their (international) business challenge on sustainability and competitiveness (contributes to PLO 1,3 & 6)
• ISB5: To develop realistic and grounded recommendations that supports the business to enhance both their sustainable and competitive position (contributes to PLO 3, 4, 5 & 6)
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25ISB1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Global Mindset and Sustainability
The course ISB is a BIP (EU Erasmus+ program) where students will develop an advice for a real-life company on how to start or enhance their competitive position using sustainable concepts like e.g. circular economy, sustainability or de-growth. Teams will be a mix from all the participating universities and the main research question: “How can contemporary durable concepts contribute to <company>  to become a more sustainable business whilst enhancing their (sustainable) competitive position?”
Students must of underpin their results:
• using the theories, models and concepts of the selected concepts,
• collecting relevant data
• finalizing with tailored analysis
• and building actionable recommendations for business
This course actively contribute to instill the development on knowledge, skills and attitude of participants on the following SDG’s: 8, 9, 11 & 12

•    demonstrates the above capability by integrating relevant concepts, and by devising relevant solutions when addressing issues of management, finance, marketing, logistics and/or HR. (ref DD2; MIBM PLO6 & PLO7)

metadata.Naam: European Business in a Global Context

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25EBG1C.outcomes:
After completing the course the student is able to:
EBG1 analyze and assess the function, structure, and dynamics of the EU (PLO 1)
EBG2 examine the role(s) of EU politics and economic policy making (PLO1, PLO3)
EBG3 appraise industries’ capabilities and environments in terms of EU related opportunities and constraints (PLO1, PLO2, PLO3, PLO4, PLO5, PLO7)
EBG4 propose corporate / business strategies based on evaluation of EU related opportunities and constraints (PLO1, PLO2, PLO3, PLO4, PLO5, PLO6, PLO7)
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25EBG1C.content:
The course covers following topics:
1. Introduction to the European Business in the Global Context:
1.1. A Portrait of Europe: key features.
1.2. European Business: structure and performance.
1.3. Europe in the lead for sustainability.
2. The EU strategies for resilient and sustainable future & international business.
2.1. The Six European Commission’s priorities for 2019-1024.
2.2. Recovery plan for Europe: opportunities for business.
2.3. A European Green Deal: opportunities for business.
2.4. Overall targets and reporting: what does it mean for business?
3. EU Energy, Climate Change, and Environment Policies: main features and implications for business organisations in the EU.
3.1. Implementation of EU Energy, Climate Change, and Environment Policies in EU countries: implications for business.
3.2. EU standards, tools and labels: implications for business.
4. EU international cooperation on climate, energy and environment and contribution to SDGs: main features and implications for international business.
4.1. EU international cooperation on climate, energy, and environment: what does it mean for international business? International Climate Finance.
4.2. EU contribution to international sustainable development goals: what does it mean for business?
5. EU digital economy, EU social economy and reforms in the EU financial sector:
5.1. A Europe fit for the digital age: what does It mean for international business?
5.2. An economy that works for people.
5.3. Reform support for the financial sector
6. EU in the world economy: opportunities and challenges for international business.
6.1. EU engagement within the European Space – relations with candidate countries and European Neighbourhood Policy: economic aspects, opportunities and challenges for businesses
6.2. EU trade relations with developed countries.
6.3. European and the BRICs: opportunities for businesses
6.4. Europe and the Least Developed Countries - trade, aid and the ACP states. Opportunities for businesses.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25PRA1C.outcomes:
1.    The student understand key concepts and theories of political risk analysis, which contributes to PLO 1.
2.    The student can identify key risks and opportunities for international business in volatile, complex and uncertain conditions, which contributes to PLO 2.
3.    The student can assess the likelihood and impact of the risks and opportunities in order to prioritize those needing attention, which contributes to PLO 3.
4.    The student can generate and evaluate different options to address the challenges, which contributes to PLO 4.
5.    The student can communicate the relative value of options and identify trip-wires to change previous decisions, which contributes to PLO 7.
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25PRA1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship and Global Mindset
International business encounters political and security factors that create risks as well as opportunities for them in volatile, complex and uncertain conditions.   This course teaches students to understand the theoretical body in political risk analysis, and to apply such knowledge, in order to assess challenges and to generate options for the company executives in managing these challenges.
This course contributes to
SDG 7, 8, 9, 11

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25EWP1C.outcomes:
1. Understanding Well-Being and Performance Theories:
Explain and critically analyze contemporary theories related to employee well-being and performance, including the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory, Self-Determination Theory, and Conservation of Resources (COR) Theory
(Contributes to PLO 1 & 2).
2.  Analyzing Organizational and Personal Factors:
Evaluate how organizational factors (e.g., leadership, HR practices, work characteristics) and personal factors (e.g., job crafting, playful work design, vitality management) influence employee well-being and job performance.
(Contributes to PLO 1 & 4)
3. Developing and Implementing Well-Being Strategies:
Apply theoretical insights to design, implement, and assess well-being initiatives that enhance employee performance and organizational effectiveness for an organization
(Contributes to PLO 2 & 5).
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25EWP1C.content:
Strategic Focus Area: Sustainability
This course offers a hands-on approach to understanding employee well-being and job performance in today’s workplaces. Students will delve into key theoretical frameworks and apply them through engaging workshops, case studies, and real-world examples. The course equips students with the skills to design and assess employee well-being programs that drive both individual and organizational performance.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25ITX1C.outcomes:
Upon completion of this course students will understand:
How to communicate effectively with tax consultants and accountants in order to recognise and understand international tax items.
the principles of international tax legislation, avoidance of double taxation and international tax planning schemes.
Issues as transfer pricing, international mergers & acquisitions, withholding taxes, tax-avoiding schemes.
PLO’s: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25ITX1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepreneurship & Global Mindset & Sustainability
Cross border business activities imply (by definition) the application of international tax regulations in order to avoid double taxation. To this end guidelines are provided by the OECD and the European Community. These result among other things in unilateral and bilateral tax treaties and EC legislation. Prospective managers to be involved with cross border activities should recognise the international tax framework and its possibilities and limitations.
The successful student acquires and understands a range of international tax issues in headlines. The student recognises (international) tax aspects arising from cross border business activities. This module focuses on the role and meaning of tax treaties for the avoidance of double taxation, OECD Guidelines, EC Directives and jurisprudence and tax planning schemes
SDG’s: 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16

The Creating Business Opportunities course is designed to equip Master-level students with conceptual frameworks and an understanding of identifying and creating business opportunities in complex environments under conditions of uncertainty. Through an entrepreneurial lens, the course delves into the theory and practice of creative destruction and disruptive innovation and their role in economic growth and sustainable economies.
The course contributes to SDGs 8, 9 and 12.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25CBT1C.outcomes:
The course learning outcomes are:
By the end of this course, students should be able to:
CBT1: Understand key contemporary business trends and their implications for marketing strategy and examine how global shifts, such as digital transformation and consumer behavior changes, are reshaping marketing tactics and creating new opportunities for businesses.
[Refers to PLO1]
CBT2: Analyze real-world case studies and emerging business models and investigate how organizations successfully adapt to market disruptions by evaluating practical examples and identifying innovative approaches to business challenges.
[Refers to PLO4]
CBT3: Evaluate the role of technology, sustainability, and innovation in business and assess how emerging technologies, sustainable practices, and a culture of innovation are driving competitive advantage and influencing long-term business success.
[Refers to PLO1]
CBT4: Develop strategic approaches to managing change in a rapidly evolving environment and formulate actionable strategies for organizations to remain adaptable, resilient, and forward-thinking while responding to shifting market dynamics and industry trends.
[Refers to PLO4]
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25CBT1C.content:
Strategic Focus Area: Global Mindset
This course explores emerging and contemporary trends in business, examining their impact on industries, organizations, and global markets. Topics include digital transformation, sustainability, globalization, innovation, and leadership in a dynamic, unpredictable, and rapidly changing business environment. The course combines theoretical insights with real-world applications, fostering critical thinking and strategic decision-making skills.
The course covers the following topics:
Week1: Introduction to Contemporary Business Trends: Overview of the contemporary business landscape, forces shaping the modern business environment, and the  role of technology, globalization, and policy changes
Week 2: Digital Transformation & Emerging Technologies: Impact of AI, Big Data, and automation on business, digital business models and platform economy, and blockchain and cybersecurity concerns
Week 3: Sustainability and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR): The role of ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) in business strategy, circular economy and sustainable business practices, and ethical leadership and corporate governance
Week 4: Globalization and International Business Trends: Trade policies, global supply chains, and geopolitics, the impact of emerging markets on global business, cross-cultural management and international leadership
Week 5: Innovation and Business Model Disruption: Disruptive innovation and market dynamics, the role of startups and venture capital in business evolution, and case studies of innovative companies (e.g., Tesla, Uber, Airbnb)
Week 6: Leadership and Organizational Change: Managing change in turbulent business environments, leadership styles for contemporary business challenges, and organizational agility and resilience
Week 7: Future Business Trends and Course Wrap-Up: The future of work: Remote work, gig economy, and workforce trends, AI and human collaboration in business decision-making, and reflection and final discussions on emerging business paradigms.
This course contributes to
SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth

Since the 80’ies and 90’ies of the previous century, stock markets have a growing impact on economic and business life. /nl/course/2026/UTVM25PPP1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship and Global Mindset
The MIBM Proposal for Professional Product will give students the opportunity to explore and integrate in length aspects of theories, methods, knowledge and skills, given along the first semester of the MIBM program. The combination of that specific content with approaches and professional practice techniques and skills  addressed in this course, will create the relevant content and educational process of the Proposal for Professional Product course. This proposal is to be executed in course Professional Product that students will do in semester 3 (P1/P2 of year 2).
The student will be exposed to knowledge, multiple techniques, methods and procedures on business- and management consulting, project/program-, risk- and change management aimed at successfully delivering the Proposal for Professional Product.
Students will deliver a proposal on how to solve a problem or exploiting an opportunity of an organizational addressing the topics mentioned before as well as realizing personal development and the intersection between them (Action Learning). Students will develop a plan on how they will gather and interpret data by using appropriate methods and tools aimed at aimed at successfully delivering of the Professional Product.
The personal development is to be made quantifiably and measurable by a section of the proposal (Personal Development section).
The student’s proposal need to be thorough, rigorous and well organized and involve undertaking systematic activities. Therefore, students have to use appropriate methods to systematically collect and interpret data, argue why the results obtained are meaningful and relevant for both the organization at hand as for personal development of the student.
The deliverable of this course is a Proposal for Professional Product.
This course contributes to the following SDG’s: 4, 8 & 9.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25ARU1.content:
The Master in International Business & Management (MIBM) programme offers students the opportunity to spend their second semester studying at Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) in Cambridge, United Kingdom. Please note there are limited places available for outgoing MIBM students.
This is a unique opportunity to achieve a truly international experience while studying, and to obtain two officially recognised international degrees within an 18 month period: Master of Business Administration (MBA) from Hanze University UAS and Master of Science in International Business (MSc) from ARU in Cambridge. The tuition fee for the Dual Degree Programme is the same as for the regular MIBM programme.

/nl/course/2026/UTVM25THE1C.outcomes:
By developing and writing the Master thesis the student will show the ability to:
CLO1: Conduct applied research into business issues in the international business context through appropriate use of research and business/management resources and methodologies to deliver practical solutions (PLO2, PLO3).
CLO2: Analyses critically, primary and secondary data to provide adequate recommendations to improve practice of a specific context (PLO2, PLO3, PLO4).
CLO3: Reflects on the results and relevance of the research to situations other than those researched (PLO8).
CLO4: Innovate and improve professional practice, based on critical appraisal of published research on business theories and practices (PLO5).
CLO5: Deal with complex and dynamic business contexts by making substantiated choices evidence-based on business theories and models (PLO2, PLO3).
CLO6: Recognize and address changes of strategic importance for the organizations due to new economic realities and propose strategies to enhance and transform business processes and articulate the implications of the progress of the proposed changes (PLO1, PLO4).
CLO7: Reflect on environmental, social, cultural and ethical aspects within business strategy, for implementation of sustainable improvement of practice (PLO6, PLO7).
CLO8: Communicate effectively to an academic and professional business community about strategic goals and potential changes in the business environment (PLO7).
CLO9: Write a research report in a scientific, clear and systematic format (PLO2, PLO7).
CLO10: Reflect on the research performance within the thesis project (PLO8).
/nl/course/2026/UTVM25THE1C.content:
Strategic Focus Areas: Entrepeneurship, Global Mindset and Sustainability
The MIBM thesis will give students the opportunity to explore and integrate in length aspects of theory or methods, knowledge and skills, given along the first year of the MIBM programme.
The combination of that specific content with research approaches and professional practice questions, will create the relevant content and educational process of the thesis course.
The thesis project is an individual assignment that is linked to a practical issue in an existing organisation, or type of organisation or to the start-up of a new organisation. The thesis research should be carried out as an assignment given by an organisation (profit or non-profit) or a professorship linked to the business issue (e.g. IBS is linked to the Knowledge Centre Entrepreneurship: KCO). Students are expected to acquire the assignment, define the problem, and formulate the research objectives and research questions themselves.
Students need to describe the theoretical framework, design a suitable methodology, gather and analyse information, draw logical conclusions and recommend realistic solutions or courses of action and /or further research.
The project should involve primary data collection by the student and should relate to the field of Marketing, Finance and Accounting, Human Resource Management, Operations Management, or Strategic Management.
The student’s investigations need to be thorough, rigorous and well organised and involve undertaking systematic research in the context of applied research. Therefore, students have to use appropriate methods to systematically collect and analyse data, argue why the results obtained are meaningful, and explain any limitations that are associated with them (Saunders, Lewis & Thornhill, 2007). MIBM students will present their Master Thesis report during a defence session.
The thesis should contribute to knowledge on the application of business theories in a real situation of practice, or to theory formation in the business field.
The MIBM thesis is an individual thesis that requires an individual assessment.
This course contributes to
SDG 7, 8, 9, 11, 12

During this project, the student will be working in peer groups of international students, and learn more about the role of a communication professional within an organisation. The research will result in a clear view on what it is like to be a communication professional. The visualisation of these result will be presented during the event #ComPro. The target audience of this event consists of the student’s own international peer group, as well as alumni students. During this event, the role of a communication professional will be approached and highlighted from different angles by various guests, and through different ‘meet & greet’ sessions with professionals in the field. To conclude, the student will be giving a media presentation for an international audience in which the role of a communication professional within an organisation is clearly highlighted.
In order to achieve all of this, the student will need to obtain good knowledge of different visions within the field of communication, hence the student will be taking a proactive role in contacting communication experts who can help the student in this respect and who can maybe play a role at the conference as well. In other words: the student will have to network in a target driven manner in order to yield him/her the necessary results.
Furthermore, the student should be aware of different forms of communication, and able to research different types of organisations which have communication professionals working for them, and understand how economical, organisational, national and international factors influence such an organisation.  In

, the student will be using different design programmes in order to produce a professional looking media presentation, and subsequently pre-test it, and present it to an audience.

In today’s complex information age, forward thinking communication professionals are continuously challenged to master the most demanding communication frontiers in creating engaging, strategic, and relevant content and information valued by their most important target groups, as well as making their client company stand out from the crowd. To this end, online marketing mix tools have an overwhelming impact on today’s society and businesses.
The student finds out how online marketing communications can be instrumental in achieving organisational objectives in a relatively complex business context from a client’s perspective. Students work in project groups and assume the role of a marketing communication advisor for a real (inter)national client company. Their task is to scan and monitor existing online content related to one of the client’s brands. Students carry out research to identify the most important market segments and the competitors. Subsequently, students develop target group profiles and brand positioning that is consistent with the core values of the client. In the final stage, students create content, making use of creative texts and visuals, and present their advice and content to the client.

/nl/course/2026/ICVP26MEE.content:
An
entrepreneurial mindset
is a set of knowledge and skills that enables people to identify and make the most of opportunities, learn from setbacks, and succeed in a variety of contexts.
In this project, students (individually or in small groups) select or create an opportunity they want to execute within
7 weeks
. The opportunity can be aimed at generating financial profit or creating a positive impact for a chosen target audience.
The project emphasizes a
growth mindset
, supporting the development of professional reflective and collaboration skills. Students progress through the steps of idea generation, opportunity recognition, opportunity screening, and action plan development, including a promotional plan (which includes video formats). To strengthen their plans, students gather insights through interviews with experts or their target audience.
The
entrepreneurial mindset
framework guiding this project is built around the following key concepts: fixed and growth mindset, developing an entrepreneurial mindset, idea generation strategies, the four pathways for opportunity recognition, opportunity screening analysis (including context analysis, market feasibility, competitive positioning, and organizational feasibility), the action mindset and action plan, as well as creative and contemporary promotion formats for the promotional plan.
During this block students learn how to create a video for their project’s promotional plan and are introduced to the fundamentals of visual storytelling, including mise-en-scène, decoupage, visual rhetoric, Gestalt principles, semiotics, and the use of the third dimension to enhance meaning and impact. Students also learn practical skills for crafting engaging video content, such as shot selection, composition, structuring a three-act storyline, storyboarding, and hands-on camera training. Together, these classes equip students to translate their ideas into clear, compelling, and visually engaging promotional material.
The professional skills
supporting the project assignments include creative thinking, pitching ideas for different purposes, and writing media products tailored to specific target groups.

/nl/course/2026/ICVB21CPI1.content:
Project - Campaign 2
Building on insights from Project 1, students work in teams to design behaviour change communication campaigns. Each team develops a comprehensive Communication Plan, starting with strategic communication objectives and outlining targeted interventions aligned with the client’s current strategy. Using the Design Thinking process—particularly Ideation and Prototyping—students create and test their campaign concepts to ensure alignment with the intended audiences.
The Campaign Plan also includes an implementation plan covering pre-launch preparations, a campaign timeline, and suggestions for post-campaign evaluation based on the agreed-upon key performance indicators.
Collaboration with the client is central to the process. Students engage the client during the ideation phase, co-create the campaign concept, and refine the prototype through feedback from both the client and target audience. The final campaign, along with all associated media products, is delivered in an agreed format, equipping the client with a ready-to-use communication strategy

In the project students create a communication campaign. To create it and different media products, they need a theoretical basis.
Communication theory is about different topics related to creating a communication campaign, such as integrated marketing communications, customer journey, objectives, budget, content and media strategies, testing and measuring, GDPR and ethics.
Media theory
addresses the role played by the visual elements in any type of media-related communication, from photography to time-based media. Students pay attention to the composition of images, the colours used, the contrast, the point of view, the typographic choice and many other characteristics, with a critical eye on the immediate meaning (denotation) and additional meanings (connotations) that might occur. Since most communication activities are nowadays implemented in an online and digital environment, the student is also asked to consider the impact of the web design best practices and ultimately the usability of the (visual) products.

Students, in teams, take the role of communication consultants and help the client with defining their problem, or the improvement/goal to be pursued. /nl/course/2026/ICVB21CSC2.content:
It is of great importance for communication professionals to have insight into organizational changes and communicative processes within organizations.
The student acquires knowledge and insight into the communicative processes of organizations. The student learns to analyze changes with the help of concepts from corporate communication theory and internal communication theory (corporate culture, employee engagement, segmenting internal audiences ). The student acquires knowledge and insight into the theories on leadership styles and development of organizations and applies this knowledge. The student also learns to look into the wider context of an organisation and assess how different external factors can influence communication using relevant knowledge from the areas of research, economics and politics.

Change communication contributes to the creation of value for an organization in change, and for its stakeholders. This includes well-founded means of communication to foster the organizational culture needed to embrace the change.
Students establish a communication strategy, make appropriate recommendations about the use of communication interventions, choose appropriate themes and formulate core messages. After completing the course, the participant will have basic knowledge of the Dutch language and culture and will have developed skills to engage in simple conversations, understand short texts, and express themselves in everyday situations.
https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/level-descriptions
/nl/course/2026/LCK25DUTA1.content:
Content
During this course the student specializes in the Dutch language and the culture of the Dutch language area (The Netherlands, Belgium, Suriname).
Topics of language skills:
Introduce yourself, asking for information, greet and say goodbye, spelling, describing people, asking what time it is, ordering and paying, thanking, asking and telling how you are, making an appointment, make a proposal, respond positively/negatively, asking/saying what you want to buy, the price and paying, asking how someone feels about something, judging positively/negatively, giving a tip, trying on and buying clothes, looking for a place to live, describing complaints, responding to doctor's questions, giving responses.
Grammar topics:
Personal pronouns (subject forms), possessive pronouns, structure of main sentences and subordinate clauses, structure of question sentences, use of definite and indefinite articles, diminutives, structure of main sentences with inversion, the use of the verb “zullen” (will, part I),  forming the plural of nouns and adjectives, imperative mood, modal verbs degrees of comparison (comparative and superlative) demonstrative pronoun (adjective use), personal pronouns (direct object forms), negation, prepositions,  the forms and use of the present perfect, the use of the indefinite pronouns “iets” and “niets”.

We expect a minimum of 80% attendance and full (100%) preparation for each lesson.

/nl/course/2026/LCK25DUI1.outcomes:
Competentie:
Duitse Taal en Cultuur: Kennis en Vaardigheden
A2 CEFR
Leeruitkomst:
Na afronding van de cursus beschikt de deelnemer over bredere kennis van de Duitse taal en cultuur, en heeft de student vaardigheden ontwikkeld om eenvoudige gesprekken te voeren over vertrouwde onderwerpen, korte teksten te begrijpen en zich begrijpelijk uit te drukken in alledaagse situaties.
https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/level-descriptions
/nl/course/2026/LCK25DUI1.content:
Inhoud:
Duitsland is één van de belangrijkste handelspartners van Nederland. Als je naar Duitsland of een Duitstalig land wilt voor stage, studie of beroep, zul je je in ieder geval op beginnersniveau moeten kunnen redden. De cursus Duits A2 biedt naast het ontwikkelen van taalvaardigheden ook inzicht in de culturele en politieke achtergronden van Duitsland. Je leert aan de hand van een aantal thema's zoals persoonlijke gegevens, studie, vakantie etc. de basis(taal)vaardigheden om je te redden in een Duitstalig land.
Het tweede gedeelte van de cursus geeft je een verdieping van de verworven kennis en vaardigheden. Je leert bijvoorbeeld hoe je tijdens een gesprek zelf adequate vragen kunt stellen en de antwoorden daarop begrijpt en vervolgens relevante vragen kunt stellen. Voorbeelden uit de praktijk helpen je daarbij. Er wordt bij deze cursus getracht zoveel mogelijk praktijksituaties na te bootsen. De nadruk ligt op het verhogen van je spreek- en schrijfvaardigheid. De grammatica heeft daarbij een ondersteunende rol. De tools hiervoor krijg je in deze cursus aangereikt.
Aan het einde van de module ben je in staat een gesprek over dagelijks veel voorkomende onderwerpen te voeren en hierover te schrijven.
Bijzonderheden:
De grammatica wordt in het Nederlands uitgelegd. Wij verwachten een minimale aanwezigheid van 80% en een volledige (100%) voorbereiding voor elke les.
Na het behalen van de cursus Duits A2 ontvang je een certificaat dat je behaalde niveau bevestigt volgens het Europees Referentiekader. Dit stelt je in staat om een Europees Taalpaspoort op te stellen, dat internationaal erkend is.
De cursussen van het HLCC worden 1 keer per week aangeboden op maandag, dinsdag, woensdag of donderdag om 16:30 uur of 18:30 uur.

hlcc@org.hanze.nl

/nl/course/2026/ICVB24GRA.content:
This year focuses on your growth from student to entry-level communication professional. You’ll show that you’re ready to enter the professional world and that you’ve mastered seven key competencies at end level (level 3). You will do this by working on various assignments and projects. We don’t assess separate tasks, instead, we look at your overall performance and development, which you will demonstrate in your portfolio. If everything meets the required standard, you will receive 60 credits (EC) for the entire year in one go.
Throughout the graduation year, you’ll follow different types of learning and receive support. Some activities you’ll do with all students, like training in writing, research, and concept development. In addition, you choose elective modules that match your interests and ambitions. You will apply what you learn straight away in projects. This helps you specialize and shape your professional profile.
Your personal and professional development is also part of your final assessment. During the year, you’ll work on learning goals that you set yourself. You will do this in a Community of Learners (CoL), supported by a mentor. You are in charge of your own learning. Feedback plays an important role in this: you’ll receive regular feedback from your mentor, clients, subject experts, and coaches. You’ll also reflect regularly on your progress.

/nl/course/2026/LCVM21MIC01.content:
In this 15 EC Module, students explore the dynamic role of a corporate communication consultant, serving as a strategic partner, providing fresh perspectives to engage diverse stakeholders, and delivering measurable impact in competitive, often global, environments.
Students will:
Advise companies on the new realities of strategic corporate communication.
Design strategies that build stakeholder trust across all platforms, internally and externally.
Use cultural insights to align corporate vision with diverse stakeholder expectations.
Develop a leadership toolkit that supports continuous professional growth.
The module is supported by applied research methodology, corporate communication theory, intercultural communication, personal leadership, and relevant workshops. Deliverables can include, but are not limited to, a professional advice report, a presentation, a research memo, a case study, and a leadership toolkit. The deliverables are assessed in a portfolio to determine how well the program learning outcomes have been achieved.
Capstone project
In a team-based capstone, students work in international groups to apply advanced knowledge of corporate communication, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills to develop a strategy that enables a brand to communicate authentically, consistently, and effectively worldwide.
Applied Research Methodology
Students improve their research skills by combining critical thinking and corporate communication. They learn to interpret data, manage the research process, solve problems, and communicate effectively.
Strategic Corporate Communication Theory
Students examine modern corporate communication concepts and apply theory to real organizational challenges. They will learn to think strategically about communication and become more confident in dealing with all aspects of corporate communication
.
Intercultural Communication
Students analyse and apply intercultural communication theories to improve corporate communication outcomes in diverse contexts. This includes recognising cultural clues, avoiding stereotypes, and adapting tone/language to the context.
Personal Leadership
Students learn how leadership development is essential for personal growth and professional success in culturally diverse environments. Students connect theory with self-awareness and consider their role as future corporate communication consultants.

Students will:
Apply media analytics to identify signals of risks, issues, and (para) crises that may threaten organisational reputation.
Use established crisis communication tools and techniques, before, during and after a crisis.
Integrate crisis communication theories and research insights into a Crisis Communication Playbook
Reflect on personal leadership and ethical decision-making in high-pressure crisis environments.
The module is supported by media analytics, issues & crisis communication theory, personal leadership and relevant workshops. Deliverables can include, but are not limited to, a Crisis Playbook, a presentation, a case study, a research memo, and a leadership toolkit. The deliverables are assessed in a portfolio to determine how well the program learning outcomes have been achieved
Capstone project
In a team-based capstone project, students work in international groups to develop a Crisis Playbook for crisis identification and management and present their strategic recommendations in a final presentation.
Issues & Crisis Communication Theory
Students analyse real situations to understand how crises develop, intensify, and can be prevented. They learn to anticipate potential risk areas and respond more effectively when a crisis does arise. They apply modern crisis communication theories to manage issues and crises effectively.
Media Analytics
Media analytics tools play an important role by providing real-time insights into online conversations. These tools enable students to track stakeholder sentiment and identify emerging issues across various media channels. Students learn to collect data through social monitoring and social listening.
Personal Leadership
Students explore different leadership styles and their own ethical foundations, particularly when addressing crises and high-stakes decisions.
