/nl/course/2026/IFCP18MAC1A.outcomes:
1. The student describes, explains and applies the planning and control cycle.
2. The student describes and explains the different types and categorizations of costs in small enterprises.
3. The student describes, explains and applies various cost accounting methods in different small enterprises and the influence on pricing and the budget.
4. The student describes, explains and applies basic variance analyses.
5. The student describes, explains and applies basic break-even, indifference and decision analyses.
/nl/course/2026/IFCP18MAC1A.content:
The module provides the fundamentals of cost accounting, or simply put, calculating the unit cost of a product or service, subject to choices and decisions made by management. All is provided within an applied form with the help of a digital learning tool called Edumundo and Excel.
Professional tasks and products:
1. Multiple cost classifications.
2. Cost allocation based on the difference between direct and indirect costs.
3. Calculations of costs per unit based on the difference between constant and variable costs.
4. Ex-ante and ex-post budgets.
5. Calculations of differences between budgets and actuals.
6. Different sorts of profit and loss-statements related to the valuation of inventories.
7. Break-even calculations.
8. Decision analyses.

/nl/course/2026/IFCP18FIN1A.outcomes:
1. The student drafts, interprets and explains financial plans and statements concerning investments, financing, budgeting and liquidity planning for small business enterprises.
2. The student computes, interprets and explains financial ratios concerning financial statements for small business enterprises.
3. The student defines and explains various forms of financing and the impact of capital structure on small business financing.
4. The student performs and explains applicable financial computations relevant to financing and investments decisions.
/nl/course/2026/IFCP18FIN1A.content:
The module Corporate Finance provides the fundamentals of financial management. Drafting and understanding financial statements, i.e. balance sheet, P&L, cash flow statements. Computing and interpreting financial ratios. Drafting and understanding financial planning and investments. Investment decisions and other financial computations. Working capital planning and cash management. Funding for investments, the capital structure of a company and the influence of leverage. Break-even analysis and general indifference computations. All is provided within an applied form with the help of Excel.
Example of professional tasks and products:
1. Compute and report financing requirements—equity and debt
2. Draft and present financial statements: balance sheet, P&L
3. Compute, interpret and present financial ratios
4. Compute cash flows and compose the cash flow statements
5. Compute and report NPV of an investment scenarios
6. Break even analysis
7. Indifference analysis
8. Liquidity requirement plan in Excel

/nl/course/2026/IFCP18BAD1A.outcomes:
1. The student describes and applies the appropriate journal entries for a trading company's financial facts and occurrences and explains the outcomes.
2. The student prepares and explains a trading company's trial balance.
3. The student describes and explains the accounting cycle.
4. The student describes and explains the interrelationship between the balance sheet, the profit and loss account and the cash flow statement.
/nl/course/2026/IFCP18BAD1A.content:
This module provides an introduction to the accounting methods of a small business enterprise. It addresses the basics of administration and bookkeeping techniques. Further, the use of the general ledger, journal entries is explained, as are all other pertinent financial statements.
Example of professional tasks and products:
1. Administrating a business
2. Using the general ledger, doing entries into the journal
3. Closing a ledger, trial balance and final statements
4. Maintaining the P&L and understanding cash flow statements

/nl/course/2026/IFCP18IFE1A.outcomes:
1. The student explains and interprets data relating to the business cycle and structure of the economy and its impact on different industries.
2. The student defines and explains the interrelationship between macroeconomic variables and the influence of government on the economy, in particular with a Keynesian model.
3. The student describes and explains structure characteristics and pricing and profit maximizing behavior within different market forms and industries.
4. The student defines and explains the role of financial institutions and the basic principles of monetary policy.
/nl/course/2026/IFCP18IFE1A.content:
Enterprises do not operate isolated, but within an constantly changing environment, also known as the external or operating environment. Developments in that external environment influence the company result. The enterprises need to align their decisions to the current and future environmental developments at a strategic level.
Insight in macroeconomic developments, like the development of the business cycle, inflation, interest and the growth of world Trade is of great importance for the business management of an enterprise. Besides that it is also very important to have an insight in the changing competitive relations in their markets; which tools are used to compete, are there entry barriers, is the market cyclically sensitive, in which phase of the product life cycle is the market? When it comes to this kind of questions we talk about meso-economic analyses. The international and financial markets and institutes are also a big component of the entire financial system, which is carried by the central banks and the monetary policy.
The course International Finance & Economics 1 offers, next to a theoretical insight in the efficiency of the economy at a both macro as meso level, also an insight in the current economic developments. These are relevant for the (inter)national operating companies and in functioning of the financial markets and the role of financial institutions.

metadata.Toetsen: International Business Law 1 - Computer, organisatie ToetsCentrum

/nl/course/2026/IFCP18IBL1A.outcomes:
1. The student describes and explains the role of the EU, economic integration, international institutions and cooperation, and how this affects legal systems.
2. The student describes and explains the various legal forms and how this affects companies.
3. The student describes and explains the VAT fiscal system in the EU and how this affects companies.
/nl/course/2026/IFCP18IBL1A.content:
This module provides an introduction to international business law and the importance of being up to date with rules and regulations to conducting business across borders. Dealing with companies in other legal and fiscal systems may pose serious problems regarding ownership of goods, but also of intellectual property. The validity of contracts may be entirely different in another country and strongly depends on local mores and beliefs regarding what constitutes an agreement. Intercultural differences are nowhere more blatantly apparent than when contracts are negotiated or disputes regarding liabilities have to be settled.
1. Comparison report on trade regulations between three different countries (one non-EU)
2. Report on legal differences between countries.
3. Report on harmonization of fiscal law in the EU.

B2:
After completing the course, the participant will have advanced knowledge of the English language, and will have developed the skills to communicate fluently and spontaneously, understand complex texts, and express themselves clearly and in detail in a variety of situations.
C1:
After completing the course, the participant will have a very advanced command of the English language. They will have developed the skills to express themselves fluently, effectively, and well-structured in both social and professional contexts, understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and use the language flexibly and appropriately for academic, professional, and informal purposes.
https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/level-descriptions
/nl/course/2026/LCK25AENG1.content:
Level:
B2 minimum, possibility to demonstrate C1
Content:
This course focuses on improving your academic English reading, writing and speaking skills. Formality and academic vocabulary are addressed in writing assignments, reading and discussing of current articles, and a presentation in which students utilise their own study background expertise. You will learn to read professional publications quicker and more efficiently by reading several publications within your own field of study, and you will expand your (mostly) passive academic vocabulary knowledge and create your own personalised academic vocabulary list with vocabulary/jargon from the Academic Word List and from your own field of study. And you will give an academic poster presentation on an academic article of your own choosing.
Details:
We expect attendance and full (100%) preparation for each lesson.
Upon passing Academic English B2, you receive a certificate confirming your attained level according to the European Framework of References, allowing you to create a European Language Passport. This passport is internationally recognized. If you perform particularly well on the course, you can be awarded a certificate indicating you are at
C1
level.
Classes are held once a week at the same time, scheduled in the late afternoon or evening.
Contact:
hlcc@org.hanze.nl

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA24.outcomes:
The student is able to use theory and process modelling to analyze operational processes and suggest improvements, within a simple intercultural context.
The student can analyze operational risks and make suggestions about mitigation, within  a simple intercultural context.
The student acts in an intercultural context in a given case. He recognizes the different ways of thinking and views on the world
The student applies advisory skills, maintains the discussion structure and deals with the behavior of the advised in such a way that the advice is accepted.
Wth the help of scientific models the student determines future cash flow (Net Present Value) and cost of capital in order to prepare investment decisions and business valuations.
The student evaluates the effects of financial leverage considering the different (hybrid) financing options (stocks, bonds, loans, lease and factoring) as well as the demands of the possible capital investors.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA24.content:
This project will require students to analyse a production company, find possible improvements and find ways to finance the proposed improvements, within an intercultural setting.
As such, the student wiill need to build on their knowledge of Operations Management and Corporate Finance to come up with the right analysis and suggestions for improvement. Students are also required to apply their knowledge of cultural differences to the findings to make them relevant in an intercultural context. Lastly, the project will have the students present their advice, based on the findings, in a way that the advice is accepted.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19ILA3.outcomes:
The learning outcomes are:
The student demonstrates the research skills of a finance professional,when (under supervision) accounting for solutions chosen with an objective helicopter view on practical issues.
The student demonstrates personal leadership and a professional and critical attitude when acting in a professional situation. He takes the financial economic context and differences between stakeholders into account. He acts according to the professional code of conduct and ethical and societal (sustainable) values.
The student demonstrates an entrepreneurial attitude within the financial economic context based on specific skills and knowledge.
The student effectively collaborates in a professional setting and aims at enhancing the quality of the outcome.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19ILA3.content:
At Hanze University researchers, education and the professional field work together in so-called Innovation Labs, where research power and field knowledge are combined to solve problems that businesses and institutions experience. In this block the students work on an assignment for a professional client participating in such an Innovation lab. The assignment will be done in groups, and supervised by a coach from the Hanze bachelor programme. Students can consult professionals from the field in the Innovation Lab. Although all the assignments have a financial and economic context, each group will receive different tasks.
At the end of the semester the research report will be graded group-wise. In addition students will be assessed on the development of their personal and professional skills, as demonstrated in a development portfolio that is individually composed. In this portfolio the student proves that s/he has met the learning outcomes by using examples from blocks 1 up to and including 4. Furthermore, the student reflects on the experience from the practical assignment during this block.
The student passes this course when the research report is graded sufficient and if s/he has proven his/her development in the area of professional skills in a criterion based interview with the coach.
This course is offered in semester 2B.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IFE2A.outcomes:
The student knows how risks can be measured on financial markets and is able to analyse the impact of risks on the pricing of financial titles.
The student is able to explain the pricing of stocks and bonds.
The student is able to identify financial risks on the financial markets, knows what financial tools can be used to control these risks and is able to describe these tools.
The student is able to analyse pricing on the international currency market and how this pricing affects the international competitiveness of companies and is able to describe how exchange rate policy can be implemented.
The student is able to describe the policy of the central bank, to interpret the instruments of monetary policy and to analyse the impact of monetary policy on the economy.
The student is able to apply statistical skills in the context of the theory of the subject.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IFE2A.content:
In this course the theory and working of central banks and financial markets will be teached and discussed.
Examples of topics are :
Central Bank policies
Money supply
Measurement of financial risks
Analyse the impact of these risks
Useful financial tools
International currency market

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA21.outcomes:
The students knows different business models and can motivate and apply the right model for a company.
The student identifies and analyses the risks that come with the chosen strategy, designs appropriate processes and finds new solutions.
The student can consider alternative trade possibilities based on a chosen strategy and in combination with the environmental influences and the financial situation.
The student recognizes risks that are caused by interest and exchange rates and covers them with financial instruments.
The student communicates in English in writing in a financial economic context. The communication is aimed at advice and forming an opinion: the student delivers an advisory report.
The student conducts a semi-structured interview, which has been prepared by making an interview setup, in which the student applies conversational techniques, applies the structure of the interview and responds to the interviewee in such a way that enough information is gathered.
The student demonstrates the research skills of a financial professional, and can motivate and argue solutions chosen from a helicopter perspective and with an objective view of practical issues.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA21.content:
During this assignment you will draw up an export strategy for an existing organization. During 10 weeks you work in groups with fellow students and via the scrum methodology.
You will apply the knowledge you have gained in the courses Strategic Management and International Finance and Economics 2. Various topics are discussed, such as internal and external analysis, the translation of a strategy into goals, interest and currency risks. The purpose of the Integral Assignment is that you gain insight into relationships between the two different fields.
To find out what the company is asking for related to an export strategy you will conduct a semi-structured interview. You demonstrate research skills of a financial professional, the outcomes of the research will has to be written in an advisory report for the organization.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA22.outcomes:
The student evaluates the management control system in relation to organization structure, responsibility centers & management style.
The student describes and explains the budget process and develops, partially, the budget using sensitivity analysis.
The student evaluates performance measurement regarding the alignment with the business strategy, the use of financial and nonfinancial performance measures and the balance between different perspectives.
The student understands and carries out the appropriate journal entries for the budget.
The student understands and carries out the appropriate journal entries for plant assets, natural resources or intangible assets.
The student can discuss, identify, explain and/or describe financial statements analysis with the ratios.
The student demonstrates IT-literacy and skills in a broad financial economic context.
The student demonstrates the research skills of a financial professional, and can motivate and argue solutions chosen from a helicopter perspective and with an objective view of practical issues.
The student individually presents (part of) the professional product and related advice to the project client in a simulated classroom setting.  The student answers client questions in a professional and well-argued manner in order to defend the professional product and the advice.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19IA22.content:
How do you get to achieve organizational goals? For this purpose, many organizations use a Planning & Control system, amongst other means. This implies that the strategy systematically is translated in plans and budgets and that performance is evaluated frequently. In this context, “Control” means that you try to manage the organization by making the right decisions based on valuable information. Valuable information, that in particular comes from a well-designed accounting system.
During this course you will use the knowledge you gained at Business Administration 2 and Management Accounting & Control 2. The assignments you will be working on apply to a company in the field. Several subjects will be covered, such as budgeting, performance measurement, journal entries and ratio analysis. The goal of the integrated assignment is that you understand relations between both fields.
You will also develop several skills during this course. To get the necessary information you will conduct an interview, taking validity and reliability into account. You will use Excel to generate useful information. When your research is done, you will persuasively hand the company your results and advice through a presentation.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19MAC2A.outcomes:
The student describes and explains the basic framework for management control systems.
The student explains the role of budgets in overall organization plans.
The student explains the role of performance measures within an organisation and computes and interprets financial performance measures such as return on investment, residual income and economic value added.
The student computes the cost of products, taking work-in-process to account, using a relevant cost accounting system and explains the consequences of choices made.
The student computes and interprets sales variances, variable cost variances and fixed cost variances. Cost variances will include (amongst others) variabel overhead (price and efficiency) variances and fixed price variances.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19MAC2A.content:
This course focusses on Performance Management. It is a follow-up to Management Accounting & Control 1.
The following subjects are covered:
Management Control
Planning and budgetting
Performance measurement
Cost accounting
Variance analysis
Using the strategy as a starting point, an organization needs to decide on which activities it should carry out. Subjects such as planning, budgeting and cost accounting are then relevant. Subsequently it is important to measure performance to find out whether the organization is on course or if it is necessary to make adjustments. In doing so, management control, performance measurement and variance analysis play an important role.
Because an organization cannot afford to focus on numbers only, the subjects will also be highlighted from the perspective of soft controls and ethics.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19BAD2A.outcomes:
The student understands and makes the appropriate journal entries for plant assets, natural resources and intangible assets.
The student understands and makes the appropriate journal entries for liabilities and the methods for the presentation and analysis.
The student understands and can record the following items related to the equity of corporations: share transactions, dividends and retained earnings.
The student understands and makes the appropriate journal entries for investments and the consolidated financial statements.
The student can prepare and analyze cash flows and a statement of cash flows.
The student can discuss, identify, explain and/or describe financial statement analyses with means of ratios.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19BAD2A.content:
In this course the focus lies on recording / administrating the firm’s business transactions and monitoring how the financial position is evolving. This will be done for several subjects like plant assets, natural resources, intangible assets, liabilities, share transactions, dividends, retained earnings and investments. Next, financial reporting is subject of this course. In the first year you learned about the balance sheet, profit and loss statement and cash flow statement as the most important financial reporting instruments. In this course we will build further on this by introducing the consolidated financial statements and a statement of cash flows. Last subject is about analysing the financial statements with using financial ratios. This is all done for drafting financial statements necessary for correctly monitoring the financial position and reporting this to management and the external stakeholders. The financial reporting is in line with the IFRS guidelines.
The course is build on the textbook 'Financial Accounting with International Financial Reporting Standards' (4th edition) by Weygandt, Kimmel and Kieso.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19SM1C.outcomes:
The student can make an internal and external analysis for an international organisation.
The student can apply strategic management models in a given case or problem for a client
The student can translate global strategic statements to concrete steps which has to be taken to reach strategic goals.
The student is able to recognise the theory on strategic management and apply it in a given case
The student is able to analyse a given case and come up with recommendations.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19SM1C.content: During this course you will learn about strategic decisions within a company. You will learn different strategic models and how to analyse and apply them to an organiztion. During a simulation you will bring the theory into practice. After the course you can translate global strategic statements to concrete steps which has to be taken to reach the strategic goals.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19CF2A.outcomes:
1. The student can use financial arithmetic to assess the extent to which an investment is financially profitable according to various selection methods (including the NCW method)
2. The student can describe the strategy of an organization and investment selection under uncertainty by means of sensitivity and scenario analysis.
3. The student can assess and advise on financing requirements, repayment capacity and dividend policy on the basis of predictions about exploitation and cash flows.
4. The student can prepare a financing plan with various possible forms of financing, taking into account the requirements of potential capital providers.
5. For valuation issues, the student can calculate the future free cash flows and the relevant cost of capital using the CAPM and WACC method.
6. The student can assess the financial position of a company by means of ratio analysis.
7. The student can describe or assess working capital management and advise on this.
8. The student is able to outline the main points of how irrational behaviour can influence prices and financial decisions (behavioural finance).
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19CF2A.content:
The module Corporate Finance 2 elaborates on the fundamentals of financial management (COF1). Drafting and understanding financial statements at market values, interpreting various valuation models and comparing values with book values. Calculating and interpreting financial ratios. Drafting and understanding financial planning and investments. Investment decisions and other financial computations. Working capital planning and cash management. Funding for investments, the capital structure of a company and the influence of leverage. Break-even analysis and general indifference computations. All is provided within an applied form with the help of Excel.
Summary of subjects:
Financial arithmetic
Financial instruments
Valuation methods
Investment analysis
Asset management
Risk and capital costs
Ratio analysis

metadata.Toetsen: Corporate Law & Taxes - Computer, organisatie ToetsCentrum

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19CLT1A.content:
This course provides a concise introduction to, and overview of, the fundamental concepts of the law of corporations and corporate tax law, both at an (inter)national and European level.
The course centers on the international company and will familiarize students with common legal and tax problems that an international company encounters.
In doing so, this course provides a broad theoretical insight into the area of corporate law and tax law.  Students will learn to recognize and understand key differences in corporate regimes, gain insight into and evaluate international contracts as well as identify and analyze tax opportunities and liabilities. The course will enable students to provide basic corporate advice on issues of risk and compliance within the area of corporate governance. Students will be able to analyze and evaluate various (inter)national legal issues and provide case-by-case recommendations. The course will encourage and require students to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills e.g. to the taxation of individuals and corporations.
Overall, the course will provide students with a broad understanding of the legal and tax risks that an international company faces. Insight into such risks as well as a proper understanding of the internal structure of a company is indispensable to the modern corporate advisor or financial professional.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19MIS2C.outcomes:
The student analyses and determines which information and data is required to control, govern and improve the organization.
The student designs and develops a database based on functional demands and standardized techniques.
The student advises on the choice for a relevant IT system which is focused on both financial as non- financial information as well as international regulations and compliance. The student also advises on the internal design of the system.
The student performs an analysis on the required management information (both recurring as well as specific) and is able to store, create and present this information in a visualization tool which incorporates geographical segregation.
The student understands the functioning of computerized algorithms, is able to apply machine learning techniques on a dataset and give an advise based on the outcomes.
The student creates a mixed integer linear programming solution that creates an optimal solution for a given case.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19MIS2C.content:
In this course students will develop the essential skills to leverage their data analytics skills. The course starts with how to collect data and how to design a database to store various sources of relational data. After this students will learn how to select IT systems for international organization and what factors are involved in selecting the right program.
Students will also learn how to visualize data in a dashboarding tool while creating a smart impact. At the same time they will also get a basic understanding of predictive analytics and machine learning. Students will learn what algorithms are and how they can use algorithms for decision making. Lastly, basic skills in optimization will be learned to solve tasks in the most cost effective manner. This means that students go through a cycle of collecting and storing data, visualizing information and predicting and optimizing organizations based on data.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB19OM1A.outcomes:
The student is familiar with process management and can describe simple operational processes.
The student is able to use theory and process modelling to analyze operational processes and suggest improvements, within a simple setting.
The student can analyze operational risks and make suggestions about mitigation, within a simple setting.
The student can draw up and assess relevant information about the control of operational processes within a simple setting.
The student is able to relate cultural aspects to operational decisions.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB19OM1A.content: Operations Management is about organizing resources in organisations to get to succesful servcies and products. Operations Management is relevant for many aspects and levels of the company and in this course we aim to provide a broad perspective on the subject. Furthermore, the cours will teach concepts and calculations for solving pratical problems within the field of operations.

/nl/course/2026/FOVB23IBS1.outcomes: The student demonstrates in a portfolio knowledge and understanding of various facets of an intercultural setting other than the country of his/her origin.
/nl/course/2026/FOVB23IBS1.content: Year 3 of the IFC programme focuses on the internship assignment and the minor. One of the assignments must be done in a country other than the country of origin (where student is passport holder of).  Students are expected to gain an intercultural experience through this. Through various assignments, the student prepares to visit another country. He or she is expected to be challenged to know the country, explore and eventually evaluate the culture of another country.

/nl/course/2026/FOVB24STG1.outcomes:
The student demonstrates the learning outcomes of
professional skills
and
responsible conduct
within the financial and economic context. This means that during the internship, the student works on professional products and/or tasks linked to subject-specific learning outcomes (level 3) of the IFC programme.
The learning outcomes are demonstrated through a combination of various behaviours and evidence.
/nl/course/2026/FOVB24STG1.content:
During the internship, you will work within the financial economic field on the learning outcomes of
professional skills
and
responsible conduct.
The internship is done individually under the supervision of your teacher supervisor and your company supervisor from the professional field. At your internship site, you will work on professional products and/or tasks. You will also work on assignments, participate in group intervisions and compile a portfolio. The exam consists of a portfolio and a criteria-based interview.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB20AL412.content:
In this last semester before the graduation project, students spend time practicing for graduation by working on so-called action-learning assignment(s) in student groups. The assignment(s) are real life professional tasks The assignment(s) will be acquired by the students themselves and will be based on one of the other theoretical subjects that are related to International Finance and Control: Business Strategy and Risk, Business Control, and Treasury Management or  Financial Accounting.
Examples of professional tasks and products:
Strategic Control Model
Responsibility/accounting model
Pricing model
Investment analysis
Budgeting model
Performance management model
Planning & Control Cycle in Service companies
Risk Management
Risk analysis
MIS reliability

/nl/course/2026/IFCB20BC1C.outcomes:
The student understands and formulates his own vision on tasks and responsibilities of a business controller and links the various areas of expertise such as business strategy, management accounting, management control and internal control and accounting information systems (ICAIS)
For an organization the student defines the need for information necessary for managing and controlling, appropriate for the internal and external context. It specifically concerns the need for information stemming from the need for management accounting and management control activities as mentioned in learning outcomes 2 and 3. The student uses standard models.
The student evaluates and designs the management control system, keeping business strategies and accountability centres into account.
As a business controller the student evaluates and designs a system of performance measurements with the aim to advise on efficiency and effectiveness of business processes.
The student  makes analyses belonging to the area of Management Accounting, including (for instance) budgetting, cost accounting, scenario analyses, gap/disparity analyses and investment calculations and het advises management on the basis of them.
The student evaluates and designs a system of risk management aimed at efficient and effective operations management, reliability of internal and external reporting and complying with laws and regulations. With these aspects in mind he describes relevant internal control risks for the organization, using valid models and theories
The student sets up administrative processes including internal control systems.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB20BC1C.content:
In this block you will take on the role of a business controller who advises the owner of a company (Spar Appel supermarket) on managerial accounting, control, business risks and management information systems. The occasion is that the company wants to expand their business (and after expansion) maintain a firm grip on the company’s financial situation now and in the future.
The course of Business Control goes deeper into the function of a business controller. The course is related to the course of Business Strategy and Risk (BSR), which goes deeper into the role of strategic partner in business as a part of the controller’s function. Led by weekly assignments in the case the student learns to perform analyses for the company to be able to make decisions. The student will advise on decisions that need to be taken. These decisions will lead to a need for information within an organization. The student will therefore set up a planning and control system based on accepted models and theories and will advise management on efficiency, effectivity and risk management. The student will make a final report on the tasks and responsibilities of the business controller and will make the link between the different aspects of the job. This report is an individual product
Example of professional tasks and products:
Strategic Control Model
Responsibility/accounting model
Pricing model
Investment analysis
Budgeting model
Performance management model
Planning & Control Cycle in Service companies
Risk Management
Risk analysis
MIS reliability
MIS relevance

/nl/course/2026/IFCB20BSR1C.outcomes:
LeveL 3
PLO1: Strategic Management
The student provides insight into an organization's national and international external environment and advises management on sustainable decisions for the organization.
The student uses various strategic models to describe the external context of an organization.
The student considers several trends, describes the effects on the external context of a company and  incorporates this into the strategy of the organization.
The student describes and  applies a theoretical framework using theories on risk management and current affairs to come up with a strategy for managing the risks of the company.
The student knows different aspects of change in an organization differentiating between transitions in design and development
PLO4: 4: Governance, Risk & Compliance
The student advises on establishing information and business processes aimed at sustainably managing risks in an organization
The student describes and assesses the risk management process and the way in which the risk management process is set up within an organization. He advises about this. This involves both the process itself and the way it is embedded in the organization.
In a case study the student manages a risk management process on a strategic level, consisting of a description and an evaluation of risks and identifying risk management measures, whereby a risk-control matrix is drawn up. He gives recommendations/advice to the organization.
The student understands the role of the strategic partner in business as part of the responsibilities and tasks of a business controller. He can formulate his own vision on this role. In a personal reflection the student describes what the importance is of a strategic partner in business for the processes of designing strategy, strategic risk management and change management in the organization.
/nl/course/2026/IFCB20BSR1C.content:
The course Business Strategy & Risk (BSR) comprises determining business strategy and concomitant risks and formulating them at an operational level.
It entails studying current theories and applying these on real case assignments in groups, mainly in accordance to the graduation research framework.
Students conduct an internal and external research of the organization based on correct methodological principles, evaluate the existing corporate strategies and risks, and subsequently formulate substantiated recommendations related to business strategy and measures for strategic risk management, based on pertinent theories.
This time we shall move from the abstract towards the concrete, by operationalizing business strategies and describing execution and tangible outcomes.
The module is related to the Business Control module coming up in the following period.
Both these modules highlight the pivoting role of a business/financial controller in an organization.
After this course you can:
Research and explore the external environment of an organization and distinguish the determining factors and trends needed to realize the firm's business strategy while controlling strategic risk.
Describe the main theories related to strategic and risk management.
Recommend measures and organizational changes in the management of business strategy and risk.

/nl/course/2026/IFCB20FA1A.outcomes:
Program outcome 7. Finance Operations and Reporting  (level 3) The student drafts and analyses external accountability reports for all stakeholders in accordance with applicable guidelines, laws and regulations which is specified into the following learning outcomes:
1.The student is able to discuss the impact of international differences on the application of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
2. The student can describe the causes of differences because of politics, culture and other reasons for differences in interpretation and discuss efforts aimed at harmonization of financial accounting standards.
3. The student is able to describe, apply and appraise the requirements of IFRS/IASB relating to items such as:
- intangible and tangible (fixed) assets
- impairments
- fixed assets
- lease
- inventories
- provisions, contingent liabilities
- revenues
- income taxes
- consolidated statements
- and others
4. The student is able to analyse and comment on parts of the financial statements:
- financial position/balance sheet
- income statement/profit and loss account
- cashflow statement
- comprehensive income and equity
whilst being aware of the needs of the users of financial statements and possible manipulations by management and interpretations of different international standards
5. The student is able to discuss and elaborate on topics such as business ethics, corporate governance, corporate social responsibility and sustainability reporting
/nl/course/2026/IFCB20FA1A.content:
SHORT DESCRIPTION
Knowledge of the requirements of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and a critical understanding of issues and alternatives, of the whys and wherefores of financial reporting in an international context.
Conceptual framework and contextual background; exploring detailed issues and problems of financial reporting for individual companies and for group and multinational companies. In-depth consideration of financial statement analysis within a dynamic international context.
Example of professional tasks and products:
Preparing (parts) of financial statements (financial position, income statement, cash flows, consolidated financial statements, currency translation)
Analysing and interpreting financial statements, whilst being aware of the needs of the users and possible manipulations by management

/nl/course/2026/IFCB20TM1A.outcomes:
Level: 3
PLO 3: Performance Management
The student selects appropriate analytical methods aimed at making sustainable decisions for an organization and applies them.
1.    The student explains how corporate bonds are valuated and estimates the credit risks on corporate debt.
2.    The student describes and explains the theory of derivatives, like options, swaps, forwards and futures
3.    The student describes the theory of exchange rates and explains how current and forward exchange rates are determined.
4.    The student applies the most important derivatives and techniques to manage interest rate risks in business situations and calculates the financial consequences of these derivatives and techniques
5.    The student applies the most important derivatives and techniques to manage exchange rate risks in business situations and calculates the financial consequences of these derivatives and techniques
PLO 5: Finance, Operations and Reporting
The student advises on financial issues, taking financial and business risks, and applicable fiscal regulations into account.
6.    The student explains and applies different methods of financial planning and working capital management
/nl/course/2026/IFCB20TM1A.content:
In this course two important aspects of the treasury function are discussed.
How to optimize a company's working capital by financial planning and working capital management
How to use derivatives, such as options, forwards, futures and swaps to hedge the credit risks, the interest rate risk and the exchange rate risks. For understanding the international risks, the working of the foreign exchange market will also be discussed in detail.

/nl/course/2026/FOVB24ASO1.outcomes:
During graduation, the student demonstrates research skills at final level (level 3). This includes the learning outcome below:
- The beginning financial professional demonstrates research skills while carrying out an assignment in the financial-economic field. The beginning financial professional does so by contributing to a feasible solution to a practical problem in a methodical, substantiated and responsible way. The beginning professional develops by critically reflecting on his own choices.
In addition, the student demonstrates part of the competence of professional advice and communication. This involves the behaviour in the field of written communication:
- You communicate in writing in an effective, clear and correct manner.
/nl/course/2026/FOVB24ASO1.content: You write a research report individually or in a duo, which is followed by an individual criterion-Based-interview (CBI). The combination of research report and CBI must show that you can complete a full research cycle. The research results in an advisory report for a client, possibly including one or more professional products. The research focuses on one or more core subjects of your study program.

The student identifies and analyzes modifiable lifestyle factors and explores potential collaborative partners within the field of preventive care with the aim of promoting healthy (physical activity) behavior. The student is able to describe these findings in a written report. Professional role: HP-1
The student demonstrates mastery of the fundamental principles and basic knowledge (the Body of Knowledge) required to successfully perform the professional role of health promoter — including ethics, rights, laws, and regulations — at proficiency level 1 (primarily factual knowledge, understanding, and reproduction). /nl/course/2026/PIVP23LP.content:
Prevention aims to promote physical, mental, and social well-being. A physiotherapist who focuses on prevention is concerned with behavioral change and focuses on people's ability to adapt and control life's social, physical, and emotional challenges.
In this course, prevention focuses on a healthy lifestyle in which aspects such as eating habits, exercise, and dealing with stress are treated. In this course, students work in small groups on various assignments. The student is given the assignment to map out the offer in the field of prevention and the wishes and needs in the field of health and well-being for a specific group of people. Physiotherapeutically relevant questions are formulated and answered. In this course, the student thus learns important preventive measures for a healthy lifestyle and the roles of various care providers, trainers, and volunteers within this range. The course is concluded with a group presentation and a group report.
This course also includes the IPE Cluster Project Health, Care & Vitality Year 1 (1 EC).
In this project, students are introduced to interprofessional collaboration in an active way by working together with various degree programs within the Health, Care & Vitality cluster. Through a shared assignment, they get to know each other better, both socially and professionally. Central to this is discovering role clarity and making use of complementary differences in perspectives and expertise.
The Meta-Model of Interprofessional Development (Reinders, 2018; Reinders & Pesut, 2022; Reinders et al., 2023) helps them understand how these different contributions come together to create effective collaboration.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25EHP.content:
In the section of the curriculum dedicated to entrepreneurship, the focus is on innovation in physiotherapy. Within the competence profile of the physiotherapist, the ability to organize and innovate becomes increasingly crucial. The dynamics in healthcare are changing, as are the needs of patients. This calls for flexibility and an expanded skill set for new healthcare providers.
At Hanze University of Applied Sciences, entrepreneurship is considered a key focal point, but it does not mean that every physiotherapist must start their own business. However, every University of Applied Sciences (HBO) student is expected to possess entrepreneurial qualities by the end of their studies.
Entrepreneurial qualities are also important in existing organizations. These qualities are necessary to continually innovate and develop new ideas to enhance physiotherapeutic care.
As an entrepreneurial physiotherapist, it is crucial to respond to the needs of the environment. To understand these needs effectively, various research methods are employed. Only when the needs are clear we contemplate possible solutions. Different techniques and methodologies are applied for this purpose, such as design thinking, moonshot thinking, and the business model canvas.
By practising and working with these methods, students are able, by the end of this module, to make an innovative contribution to the organization of healthcare.
This course includes the
IPE Cluster Project Health, Care & Vitality – Year 2
Collaboration in healthcare contributes to the quality of care for patients and clients, but it is not always self‑evident. Healthcare professionals act from a strong professional identity, which guides their choices and decisions. Effective collaboration requires insight into each other’s roles, perspectives, and areas of expertise, so that role clarity can develop and more can be achieved together.
In this project, students use the Meta-Model of Interprofessional Development (Reinders, 2018; Reinders & Pesut, 2022; Reinders et al., 2023). They work through: Phase 0 (professional identity), Phase 1 (shared problem domain), and Phase 2 (combining priorities and alternatives), with the aim of strengthening collaboration and making use of the added value of each other’s differences.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB24RI2.content:
Clients and health insurers expect physiotherapists to provide optimal care. The Royal Dutch Society for Physical Therapy (KNGF) defines optimal care as care based on the best available evidence from three pillars of Evidence Based Practice (EBP): Scientific literature; Patient expectations, and Provider experience. Through Shared Decision Making (SDM), the physiotherapist can bring together these 3 pillars and collaboratively develop a treatment plan with a patient. SDM is a method of communication where mutual information exchange is essential.
In the course Research and Innovation 2, students will apply SDM, based on the 3 pillars of EBP. The scientific literature pillar is addressed by writing a review article on physiotherapeutic treatment, systematically searching the scientific literature, and working on accurately interpreting scientific articles. Patient expectations are determined through qualitative research. For the last pillar, the experience gained from physiotherapy education and practice is utilised. At the end of the semester, students conclude with an SDM conversation and a presentation in which they explain and justify their SDM process and the ultimate treatment plan they have arrived at.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB26PD2JI2.content:
PD2
The education focuses on the Study and Professional Development of students. Throughout the entire physiotherapy program, the student develops their own professional identity. Professional identity is about who you are, what is distinct about you, making you recognizable to others, and enabling you to stand firm in challenging situations. Professional identity develops through interaction between the student, the program, and the immediate environment. Professional identity forms gradually. Personal and professional development are closely interconnected, with personal development influencing, colouring, and shaping professional development, and vice versa.
Directly linked to the Professional Development curriculum is Junior Internship 2.
JI2
The work of a physiotherapist involves examining (and treating), guiding, and coaching clients with health problems. During the study in the physiotherapy program, the student learns concepts and skills to be used in their future work as a physiotherapist. By properly completing the unit "Junior Internship 2," the student develops competencies at level 2 to deal with "real clients." In this unit, students' clinical reasoning is directly linked to performing relevant physiotherapeutic skills for the given patient, and interacting with the client goes beyond applying technical skills.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25PC9PE.content:
The course Pediatric Physiotherapy consists of 2 parts.
Part 1:
Theoretical and practical instruction will be given in the field of physiotherapy for children. The main focus of this module is the development (motoric and social-emotional) and locomotor learning of children (ages 0 to 18 years). We will discuss specific pediatric physiotherapeutic clinimetric tools and observational skills. Observational skills will be tested by means of a presentation. When relevant, we will work with patient demonstrations. The module will end with a practical test in which skills and clinical reasoning are tested by means of case study.
Part 2:
A number of specific conditions will be discussed in this module. Attention will be paid to the development of these conditions and the role of a pediatric physiotherapist. The module will end with a practical test in which skills and clinical reasoning are tested by means of case study.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25PC9AD.content:
Employees have to work longer and experiencing more and more work pressure. The physiotherapist is important in analyzing and reducing mental and physical stress factors that are related to work. In addition, the physiotherapist is competent in different mental and physical stress-reducing techniques. During various previous courses, the student has gained experience in reduced participation by means of written cases. Within this course the student performs a work analysis at a person who works with complaints.
Also physiotherapeutic methods that can be applied to nonspecific musculoskeletal problems such as back pain, neck pain and shoulder pain, which often are workrelated, will be discussed.
Complex work-related health problems are also addressed. This enables the student to better respond to complex work-related complaints that put the sustainable employability of workers under pressure. Attention is paid to both acute complaints and care in the post-rehabilitation phase, in collaboration with other healthcare professionals

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25PD3AC.content:
This course consists of two components: Professional Development 3 and Ageing & Concepts.
During this period, the student further develops their professional identity.
The student learns to provide high-quality client care in an honest, sincere, and engaged manner. They take responsibility for their actions and carefully maintain a balance between personal and professional roles. The student is open to feedback, acts transparently, and operates with a correct professional attitude. This is documented through a reflection report.
In addition, the student learns to present a well-supported position related to Ageing & Concepts, lifespan psychology, ethics, gender diversity, or limited health literacy in physiotherapeutic care. The position must be clear and relevant and is presented using an infographic.
Furthermore, the student learns to debate an ethical dilemma/case from practice.
The student develops skills in critical thinking, reasoning, communication, listening, collaboration, problem-solving, research, and perspective-taking. These are essential skills for physiotherapists to effectively communicate and work with other healthcare professionals.

The student can read, evaluate, and interpret (English-language) research articles. Professional Role: IP, Level 2.
Under the supervision of a lecturer and in collaboration with fellow students, the student can design and conduct a quantitative, practice-oriented research project, analyze and interpret the results, and write a research report. Professional Role: SWP, IP, Level 2.
Under the supervision of a lecturer and in collaboration with fellow students, the student can design and conduct a qualitative, practice-oriented research project, and analyze and interpret the results. Professional Role: SWP, IP, Level 2.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25RI3.content:
To provide the best possible care, it is important for physiotherapists to be investigative, critical, and innovative. Physiotherapists must demonstrate to clients and health insurers that their physiotherapy interventions are well-founded from a scientific perspective. The ability to properly interpret and critically assess the scientific value of research and literature is a key skill in this regard. It is also important for physiotherapists to be able to use their investigative skills to facilitate developments and innovations.
In R&I 3, students work in a journal club for the first few weeks to gain insight into the differences between qualitative and quantitative research and to develop a deeper understanding of the reliability of quantitative research and inferential statistics. The articles discussed cover current, relevant physiotherapy topics.
Students are then introduced to conducting research using quantitative and qualitative research designs. Each student, in collaboration with fellow students and under the supervision of the tutor, designs and conducts a quantitative and a qualitative study. The topics for these studies are either devised by the students themselves or provided by external parties. The topics are relevant to physiotherapy and ultimately result in well-founded advice/recommendations and/or the impetus for a design, product, or innovation.
For the quantitative research, a research question will be formulated, an appropriate method and assessment selected, and data collection and analysis conducted. For the qualitative research, a research question will be formulated and at least two in-depth interviews per person will be conducted, transcribed, and coded. Students will learn to process and interpret collected data and draw appropriate conclusions. The qualitative research and its results will be presented in an oral presentation, and the quantitative research and its results will be presented in a research report.
In meetings with a supervising instructor, the progress of the research will be discussed and there will be opportunity for (peer) feedback on interim products. In addition, supporting education is offered, such as an SPSS practical and a lesson in scientific presentations.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB26SI1.content:
The internships within the physiotherapy programme are aimed at developing, in practice, the professional roles characteristic of a beginning physiotherapist. The senior internships and the graduation internship together form a learning process in which the student deepens and broadens their professional role.
During the senior internships, the student learns to take responsibility for their own actions and works under supervision to strengthen the professional roles, with emphasis on the roles of healthcare provider and collaborator.
In the graduation internship, the focus shifts to functioning at final‑qualification level. Here, the student is expected to act independently and professionally, integrating all roles. The student demonstrates the ability to analyse complex problems, select appropriate interventions, and carry them out responsibly.
The programme includes two senior internships and one graduation internship.
Throughout the senior internships and the graduation internship, the student works towards level 3 in all seven professional roles of the physiotherapist within the context of professional practice. The final level of the graduation internship is level 3, the level of a beginning practitioner.
During the first senior internship, which lasts 10 weeks, the student works on several professional products alongside the internship itself. This includes writing a CAT, a CASE (and presenting the CASE at the internship site as part of an Intercollegial Consultation – Case Presentation), and submitting various patient documentation assignments.
During Senior Internship 2, the student works on the graduation assignment alongside the internship.
During the graduation internship, the student works towards a high degree of independence and complexity.

/nl/course/2026/PIVB25ASO.content:
During this course, students work on a graduation assignment that requires applied scientific/practice-oriented research. The graduation assignment is related to the physiotherapy domain and the aim is to have students work on an assignment from the field. Knowledge and skills acquired in R&I courses are applied at the final level while working on the graduation assignment.
In the first half of the course, students work on a research plan. This is submitted for feedback halfway through the trajectory. In the second half of the course, students carry out the research and the results are recorded in the form of a Bachelor's thesis. The course is concluded with an individual final presentation followed by a criterion-based interview.
Admission requirements:
To be admitted to the Graduation Assignment, students must have completed all educational units from the first and second year of study. In addition, O&I from year three must have been successfully completed. Finally, internship 1 must have been completed.

Studenten ontwikkelen een eigen kunstpedagogische visie in dialoog met actuele pedagogische theorie, de analyse van kunsteducatieve praktijken en de eigen artistieke signatuur. Vanuit diverse benaderingen in de kunsteducatie, waaronder de verbeeldingsrijke dialoog, ontwerpen en beproeven zij kunsteducatieve interventies voor nieuwe contexten. /nl/course/2026/MJDM26OP2.content: In deze onderwijseenheid staan het onderzoekend vermogen van de student en de verbinding tussen onderzoek, artistieke signatuur en educatie centraal. Studenten werken, samen met anderen, aan de versterking van het kunsteducatieve veld in brede zin. Zij ontwikkelen een eigen, onderbouwde positie ten aanzien van een actueel vraagstuk uit de kunsteducatieve praktijk, waarbij zij vertrekken vanuit hun eigen ervaring, interesses en ambities. Studenten kiezen voor hun individuele project uit drie routes die elk een eigen benadering van onderzoekend handelen vertegenwoordigen: artistiek onderzoekend, onderzoekend ontwerpen of onderzoeken & positioneren. Binnen de gekozen route formuleren zij hun vraagstuk op basis van relevante theorieën en diverse bronnen, en verkennen zij dit verder in de praktijk of op beschouwende wijze. De opbrengsten hiervan worden op een transparante, navolgbare en ethisch verantwoorde manier gedocumenteerd, passend bij de gekozen route. Het onderwijs bestaat uit een mix van onderzoeksvaardigheden en de verdieping en integratie van de perspectieven van de kunstenaar en de educator, zoals deze ook in het eerste jaar zijn aangeboden. In trainingen en gastcolleges ontwikkelen studenten bovendien de communicatieve vaardigheden die nodig zijn om hun inzichten overtuigend te presenteren.

/nl/course/2026/MJDM26PR2.content: Binnen de Master Kunsteducatie staat de individuele professionaliseringsvraag van de student centraal. In samenspraak met de studiecoach geven studenten richting aan hun studieroute, zodat persoonlijke leerdoelen doelgericht en samenhangend worden ondersteund. Medestudenten leveren een bijdrage via advies en peerfeedback, wat de versterking van het professionele profiel en de positionering als master bevordert. De Profileringsruimte, een vrije keuzeruimte van 5 EC, biedt studenten de mogelijkheid om eigen accenten te leggen binnen de opleiding. Zij kunnen kiezen voor cursussen, bij‑ of nascholing binnen het eigen werkveld, conferentiebezoek, deelname aan seminars, betrokkenheid bij lectoraatsprojecten, ontwikkelstages of verdieping van het praktijkonderzoek. Zo geven zij de masteropleiding een doelgerichte en persoonlijke verdieping. In de masterbiografie en het masterassessment laten zij zien welke rol de profilering gespeeld heeft in hun positionering als master in kunsteducatie.

/nl/course/2026/MJDM26NV2.content: Deze onderwijseenheid beslaat beide leerjaren, met een zwaartepunt in het tweede jaar, en richt zich op omgevingsgericht handelen. Studenten ontwikkelen inzicht in (internationale) maatschappelijke ontwikkelingen en verkennen hoe zij als kunsteducatief professional kunnen bijdragen aan vernieuwing van het werkveld. De onderwijseenheid bestaat uit vier samenhangende lijnen. De eerste behandelt systemische veranderingsprocessen, ondersteund door veranderkundige theorieën en Futures Literacy. De tweede richt zich op netwerkontwikkeling binnen het noordelijke werkveld, via door studenten gekozen en door de opleiding georganiseerde activiteiten. Daarnaast verkennen studenten tijdens een internationale excursie relevante kunsteducatieve en culturele praktijken in een Europese context. In het masterassessment brengen zij voor het voetlicht hoe deze activiteiten hebben bijgedragen aan hun professionele ontwikkeling en omgevingsgericht handelen. Tot slot organiseren zij, bij voorkeur met de medestudenten, een werkveldevenement rond een actueel thema, dat de dialoog tussen opleiding en praktijk versterkt en bijdraagt aan hun positionering als master in kunsteducatie.

Deze module levert een bijdrage aan de volgende leeruitkomsten op propedeuse-niveau.
LOL Pedagogisch handelen
LOL (Vak)didactisch handelen
LOL (Vak)inhoudelijke expertise ALO
LOL (Vak)inhoudelijke expertise Pabo
LOL Onderzoekend handelen
LOL Professionele identiteit
/nl/course/2026/ALVP25OIO1.content:
Inhoud van het studieonderdeel:
De student werkt gedurende dit studieonderdeel aan zijn ontwikkeling op de zes leeruitkomsten, gekoppeld aan de vijf landelijke leeruitkomstgebieden, waarbij de leeruitkomst (vak)inhoudelijk expertise een deel A en B heeft (ALO en Pabo). De student verzamelt bewijsstukken om de ontwikkeling op de leeruitkomsten aan te tonen.
De student krijgt op de opleiding verschillende lessen aangeboden waarbij de oriëntatie op de leerling en het beroep centraal staat.
Gedurende het semester maakt de student kennis met het zoeken, verwerken en presenteren van literatuur om een beeld te krijgen van het toekomstige werk(veld). Ook werkt de student in samenwerking met medestudenten toe naar de uitvoering van een project op een basisschool. Daarnaast leert de student enkele dagen op de leerwerkplek, zowel in de klas als in de zaal. Tijdens deze ervaring op de leerwerkplek kijkt de student in de klas met een groepsleerkracht en in de zaal bij een vakleerkracht bewegingsonderwijs. De focus is hierbij het ontdekken van het onderwijs, de leerlingen en de leerkrachten in het basisonderwijs, dit gebeurt door het afnemen van een interview en het doen van verschillende observaties. Daarnaast assisteert de student waar mogelijk bij lessen. Het is nog niet vereist om (zelfstandig) les te geven op de leerwerkplek. Naast de stage op de leerwerkplek, loopt de student een sportstage. Tijdens de sportstage geeft de student (zelfstandig) drie trainingen bij een sportvereniging naar keuze.
Naast de werkvormen op de opleiding krijgen studenten in een outdoorsetting (outdoorexperience) zicht op wie zij zijn als individu en binnen het team.
Uiteindelijk maakt de student een ontwikkelverslag waarin de student terugblikt op de verschillende leeruitkomsten met behulp van opgedane ervaringen en gemaakte bewijsstukken.
Opzet van de colleges:
Er worden werkcolleges aangeboden, waarbij de studenten begeleiding krijgen op de ontwikkeling op de zes leeruitkomsten en de daarbij horende bewijsstukken.
Opzet van de toetsing:
De student maakt een portfolio waarin de ontwikkeling op de zes leeruitkomsten zichtbaar wordt gemaakt. Op basis van een portfolio assessment wordt een beoordeling gegeven en ontvangt de student 9EC bij een voldoende beoordeling. Daarnaast neemt de student tijdens deze module deel aan de outdoorexperience, bij actieve participatie aan deze experience ontvangt de student 1EC.
Literatuur en eventuele kosten:
Tijdens deze module wordt er deelgenomen aan een outdoorexperience. Hier zijn kosten aan verbonden.
Literatuur wordt tijdens de lessen aangereikt en er is verplichte literatuur (zie boekenlijst).

/nl/course/2026/ALVP25TAAL1.outcomes:

X (Vak)didactisch handelen
X (Vak)inhoudelijke expertise Pabo
De leerdoelen bij deze module zijn:
1. De student kent de wettelijke kaders voor taalonderwijs (kerndoelen, tussendoelen, referentieniveaus).
2. De student kent de begrippen met betrekking tot mondelinge taalvaardigheid en jeugdliteratuur uit de kennisbasis Taal.
3. De student voert, naar aanleiding van de gelezen artikelen, gesprekken met medestudenten en docent over de inhoud ervan met als doel begripsverhoging en uitbreiding van het didactisch repertoire.
4. De student voert met medestudenten en docent gesprekken waarin de literaire competentie wordt aangetoond.
5.
De student voert activiteiten uit/maakt opdrachten gericht op de geletterdheidsontwikkeling en mondelinge taal.
6. De student leest toegepast wetenschappelijke teksten op 4F-niveau over mondelinge taalontwikkeling en jeugdliteratuur/leesbevordering in het basisonderwijs.
/nl/course/2026/ALVP25TAAL1.content:
Inhoud van het studieonderdeel:
In de module Taal 1 maakt de student kennis met de verschillende domeinen van taal binnen het basisonderwijs. In de module wordt er vakdidactische kennis opgedaan op het gebied van mondelinge taalontwikkeling en jeugdliteratuur. De student maakt kennis met de taalgroeimiddelen en het vertel-eens-gesprek en oefenen met voorlezen. Tevens wordt er gewerkt aan de eigen vaardigheid taal van de student door middel van het lezen van toegepast wetenschappelijke artikelen en recente jeugdliteratuur.
Opzet van de colleges:
De student volgt hoor- en werkcolleges. Een deel van de opdrachten die ingeleverd dient te worden, wordt ook behandeld in college (voorlezen/vertel-eens-gesprek/boekenmarkt).
Opzet van de toetsing:
De student levert een portfolio in waarin alle opdrachten die gedurende het semester worden opgestart en uitgevoerd worden aangeleverd.
Literatuur en eventuele kosten:
Tijdens deze module wordt er gewerkt met verplichte literatuur zoals ook vermeld op de boekenlijst. Tevens leest de student meerdere jeugdboeken die geleend kunnen worden bij de mediatheek/bibliotheek of zelf aangeschaft dienen te worden.

/nl/course/2026/ALVP25REW1.content:

TOETS-01
In deeltoets TOETS-01 wordt de student vaardig in inhoud en didactiek binnen het domein Hele getallen.
Binnen de module Rekenen en wiskunde - Hele Getallen oriënteert de student zich op het rekenonderwijs zoals dat wordt gegeven in het basisonderwijs.
De student leert de leerlijnen van het domein Hele Getallen kennen, het daarbij behorende begrippenapparaat en leert didactisch te handelen.
De student ontwikkelt zijn eigen professionele gecijferdheid en leert deze in te zetten ten behoeve van het ontwikkelen en het geven van onderwijs.
De student krijgt inzicht in welke materialen en bronnen beschikbaar zijn, inclusief digitale, om onderwijs binnen het domein Hele Getallen te ontwikkelen

•           Aanvankelijk rekenen

•           Voortgezet rekenen
•           Leren en onderwijzen van rekenen-wiskunde

Er is een schriftelijke toets waarin zowel didactiek als eigen vaardigheid aan bod komen.
